docs.title: Welcome to VPX Game Logic Framework
docs.text: The VPX Game Logic Framework (GLF) is a powerful and flexible framework for creating original virtual pinball tables using the VPX platform. It provides a comprehensive set of game logic components that enable you to build sophisticated pinball games without writing extensive code.

docs.title: About This Framework
docs.text:
GLF is inspired by The Mission Pinball Framework for real and homebrew machines. Many game logic commands mirror MPF concepts. GLF configures VPX through VBScript and can export MPF YAML; compatibility depends on the component. Read Configuration and YAML before adapting examples between the two runtimes.

One of the key goals of this project is to provide a standalone set of game logic devices that doesn't require users to install and run the MPF bridge for VPX, simplifying the development process.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Virtual Devices: Comprehensive support for flippers, bumpers, drop targets, magnets, and more
  • Game Modes: Flexible mode system for creating complex game rules and progression
  • Event System: Powerful event-driven architecture for game logic
  • Player Management: Track player scores, achievements, and high scores
  • Light Control: Advanced lighting effects and animations
  • Backbox Displays: Options for segment displays to full LCD Displays

docs.title: Learning guides
docs.text: Start with Getting Started, then follow the game lifecycle, complete timed mode and multiball walkthrough. For presentation and recovery, see Displays and Godot, sound setup, ball search and debugging.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Installation: Follow the Installation Guide to set up GLF
  2. Tutorials: Start with our Build Your First GLF Game to learn the basics

docs.title: Achievement tracking and implementation status
docs.text: The current scripts/src/commands/achievements.vbs is unfinished. Its Complete() method contains only a TODO, and its listener registration names AchievementsEventHandler while the function in that file is named AchievementsHandler. The mode API does not expose an Achievements collection. Do not treat this file as a working configurable achievement device.

docs.title: Track a completed feature with player state
docs.text:
For a simple once-per-player award, initialize a custom variable during configuration:

Glf_SetInitialPlayerVar "challenge_achievement", 0

Inside a mode that is active when the completion event arrives:

With .VariablePlayer()
    With .EventName("challenge_complete{current_player.challenge_achievement == 0}")
        With .Variable("score")
            .Action = "add"
            .Int = 50000
        End With
        With .Variable("challenge_achievement")
            .Action = "set"
            .Int = 1
        End With
    End With
End With

The condition is evaluated before that entry's updates. On subsequent completion events, the flag prevents another award. The flag belongs to each player and resets for a new game. This example awards an additional 50,000 if used alongside the complete-mode tutorial's existing completion award; remove one award if you want only one.

Use shots and profiles for visible progress or a state machine for multi-stage qualification. Use a persistent machine variable only if the achievement should be shared and retained between sessions.

This is a supported composition of existing components, not a completed implementation of GlfAchievements. Test multiple players and repeated completion events before using it in a rule set.

docs.title: Auto-Fire Configuration
docs.text: The auto-fire configuration allows you to set up and customize auto-firing devices in your pinball machine. Auto-fire devices are used to automatically fire coils or other devices when triggered by switches or events. Examples include Pop Bumpers, Slingshots

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic auto-fire configuration
With CreateGlfAutoFireDevice("left_sling")
    .Switch = "s_LeftSlingshot"
    .ActionCallback = "LeftSlingshotAction"
    .DisabledCallback = "LeftSlingshotDisabled"
    .EnabledCallback = "LeftSlingshotEnabled"
    .DisableEvents = Array("kill_flippers")
    .EnableEvents = Array("ball_started","enable_flippers")
    .ExcludeFromBallSearch = False
End With

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
• Switch: String name of the switch that triggers the auto-fire (Default: Empty)
  • ActionCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the auto-fire is triggered (Default: Empty)
  • EnabledCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the auto-fire is enabled (Default: Empty)
  • DisabledCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the auto-fire is disabled (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EnableEvents: Array of event names that will enable the auto-fire (Default: Array("ball_started"))
  • DisableEvents: Array of event names that will disable the auto-fire (Default: Array("ball_will_end", "service_mode_entered"))

docs.title: Ball Search Settings
docs.text: • ExcludeFromBallSearch: Boolean indicating whether to exclude this device from ball search operations (Default: False)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this device (Default: False)

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The auto-fire device system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • auto_fire_coil_{device_name}_activate: Triggered when the auto-fire device is activated
  • auto_fire_coil_{device_name}_deactivate: Triggered when the auto-fire device is deactivated

Replace {device_name} with your actual auto-fire device name.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, auto-fire devices are configured with: - Enabled on ball_started event - Disabled on ball_will_end and service_mode_entered events - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Ball Device Configuration
docs.text: The ball device configuration allows you to set up and customize ball devices in your pinball machine. Ball devices are used for scoops, physical ball locks, staging areas. Anywhere you want to hold a ball on the table.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic ball device configuration
With CreateGlfBallDevice("scoop")
    .BallSwitches = Array("s_scoop1")
    .EjectTimemout = 2000
    .EjectCallback = "ScoopEjectCallback"              ' Name of the callback function for ball device
End With

Each device will have a Eject Callback setting. This calls your defined function / sub when the ball should be ejected from the device. In a real pinball machine this would be the coil firing to eject the ball. In VPX, you need to implement this function to virutally kick the ball out from the device. Below is an example of how to you could do that.

Sub ScoopEjectCallback(ball)
    Dim ang, vel
    If s_scoop1.BallCntOver > 0 Then 'Check if the ball is positioned on the switch / kicker
        ang = 14.8 + ScoopAngleTol*2*(rnd-0.5) 'generate some randomness to the angle
        vel = 70.0 + ScoopStrengthTol*2*(rnd-0.5) 'generare some randomness to the velocity
        KickBall ball, ang, vel, 0, 0 'actually kick the ball
        SoundSaucerKick 1, s_Scoop 'play a sound to simulate the coil firing
    Else
        SoundSaucerKick 0, s_Scoop 'play a sound if even if the ball wasn't on the switch (failed kick)
    End If
    DOF 109, DOFPulse 'Optionally call a DOF event.
End Sub

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
• BallSwitches: Array of switch names that detect balls in the device (Default: Empty Array)
  • EjectCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the ball device ejects a ball (Default: Null)

docs.title: Ejection Control
docs.text:
• EjectTimeout: Integer specifying the timeout in milliseconds for ejection (Default: 1000)
  • EjectEnableTime: Integer specifying the enable time in milliseconds for ejection (Default: 0).
  • MechanicalEject: Boolean indicating whether the device uses mechanical ejection (Default: False)
  • DefaultDevice: Boolean indicating whether this is the default ball device (Default: False)
  • PlayerControlledEjectEvent: String name of the event that triggers player-controlled ejection (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EjectAllEvents: Array of event names that will trigger ejection of all balls (Default: Empty Array)
  • EjectTargets: Array of target names that will trigger ejection timeout when activated (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Ball Tracking
docs.text:
• EntranceCountDelay: Integer specifying the delay in milliseconds before counting a ball as entered (Default: 500)
  • ExcludeFromBallSearch: Boolean indicating whether to exclude this device from ball search operations (Default: False)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this device (Default: False)

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The ball device system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • balldevice_{device_name}_ball_enter: Relay event triggered when a ball is entering the device (can be claimed by other systems)
  • balldevice_{device_name}_ball_entered: Triggered when a ball has successfully entered the device
  • balldevice_{device_name}_ball_exiting: Triggered when a ball is exiting the device
  • balldevice_{device_name}_ball_eject_success: Triggered when a ball has been successfully ejected from the device

Replace {device_name} with your actual ball device name.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The ball device system automatically manages ball tracking and ejection based on configured switches
  • Eject callbacks receive a ball parameter (can be Null for enable time callbacks)
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track ball device state changes
  • Ball devices can be configured to eject balls during specific game modes using EjectAllEvents
  • The system prevents multiple ejection operations from overlapping
  • Ball tracking is always enabled and managed automatically
  • The entrance count delay helps prevent false ball detection
  • Mechanical ejection mode uses timeouts to track successful ball exits
  • Player controlled ejection allows manual triggering via events
  • Eject targets can be used to trigger ejection timeouts when specific targets are hit

docs.title: Ball holds
docs.text: A ball hold claims balls entering named ball devices and releases them on rule events. Use it to keep a ball in a scoop during an award or selection. Use a multiball lock when you need lock qualification and replacement-ball behavior.

docs.title: Configure a scoop hold
docs.text:
First create a ball device named scoop with a working eject callback. Inside a mode that remains active for the hold's lifetime:

With .BallHolds("scoop_award")
    .BallsToHold = 1
    .HoldDevices = Array("scoop")
    .EnableEvents = Array("enable_scoop_award")
    .DisableEvents = Array("disable_scoop_award")
    .ReleaseAllEvents = Array("scoop_award_finished")
End With

Enable the hold before the ball enters. The hold listens to balldevice_scoop_ball_enter, claims available balls, and prevents the device's normal unclaimed-ball path from releasing them. Post scoop_award_finished after the award presentation. Mode deactivation disables the hold and releases held balls.

Dark Chaos uses this pattern in scripts/src/game/modes/base.vbs with scoop_hold and explicit enable, disable and release events.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Property Meaning / default BallsToHold Capacity across the configured hold devices; default 0, so set it explicitly HoldDevices Array of registered ball-device names; default empty EnableEvents Enable the hold on these events; without any, mode activation enables it DisableEvents Disable and release all held balls ReleaseAllEvents Release everything; tilt is registered by default ReleaseOneEvents Release one held ball ReleaseOneIfFullEvents Release one only when the hold is full Debug Enable component logging

Release-event setters add entries; the built-in tilt release remains when you add your own events. Avoid registering the same release key twice.

docs.title: Events and runtime values
docs.text:
ball_hold_scoop_award_held_ball carries balls_held for that claim and total_balls_held for the hold. ball_hold_scoop_award_full carries balls. Read the count with device.ball_holds.scoop_award.balls_held in supported runtime expressions.

Test release after success, cancellation, tilt and mode stop. Do not leave a presentation waiting indefinitely while it owns the ball. For multiple claims into the same device, test against the current implementation: its internal hold queue is keyed by device name, so repeated entries are not a general per-ball queue.

Source: scripts/src/commands/ball-hold.vbs. Related: ball devices, ball search, events.

docs.title: Ball Save Configuration
docs.text: The ball save configuration allows you to set up and customize ball saving mechanisms in your pinball machine. Ball saves are used to prevent players from losing balls too quickly and can be configured to work within specific game modes.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic ball save configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .BallSaves("ball_save_name")
        .ActiveTime = 6000                ' Time in milliseconds the ball save is active
        .EnableEvents = Array("event1")   ' Events that enable the ball save
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced ball save configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .BallSaves("ball_save_name")
        ' Timing settings
        .ActiveTime = 6000                ' Time in milliseconds the ball save is active
        .GracePeriod = 2000               ' Additional time after active time before disabling
        .HurryUpTime = 3000               ' Time before active time ends to enter hurry-up state

        ' Event settings
        .EnableEvents = Array("event1", "event2")           ' Events that enable the ball save
        .DisableEvents = Array("event3", "event4")          ' Events that disable the ball save
        .TimerStartEvents = Array("event5", "event6")       ' Events that start the ball save timer

        ' Ball save behavior
        .AutoLaunch = True                ' Whether to automatically launch the saved ball
        .BallsToSave = 2                  ' Number of balls to save before disabling

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True                     ' Enable debug logging for this ball save
    End With
End With

docs.title: Timing Settings
docs.text:
• ActiveTime: Time in milliseconds the ball save is active (Default: Null)
  • GracePeriod: Additional time after active time before disabling (Default: Null)
  • HurryUpTime: Time before active time ends to enter hurry-up state (Default: Null)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EnableEvents: Array of event names that will enable the ball save (Default: Empty Array)
  • DisableEvents: Array of event names that will disable the ball save (Default: Empty Array)
  • TimerStartEvents: Array of event names that will start the ball save timer (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Ball Save Behavior
docs.text:
• AutoLaunch: Boolean indicating whether to automatically launch the saved ball (Default: False)
  • BallsToSave: Integer indicating the number of balls to save before disabling (Default: 1)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this ball save (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Ball Save Example
docs.text:
' Basic ball save configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .BallSaves("new_ball")
        .ActiveTime = 6000
        .EnableEvents = Array("new_ball_active")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Ball Save Example
docs.text:
' Advanced ball save configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .BallSaves("multiball_save")
        ' Timing settings
        .ActiveTime = 10000
        .GracePeriod = 3000
        .HurryUpTime = 2000

        ' Event settings
        .EnableEvents = Array("multiball_started")
        .DisableEvents = Array("multiball_ended")
        .TimerStartEvents = Array("multiball_ball_launched")

        ' Ball save behavior
        .AutoLaunch = True
        .BallsToSave = 3

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The ball save system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • {ball_save_name}_enabled: Triggered when the ball save is enabled
  • {ball_save_name}_disabled: Triggered when the ball save is disabled
  • {ball_save_name}_timer_start: Triggered when the ball save timer starts
  • {ball_save_name}_grace_period: Triggered when the ball save enters grace period
  • {ball_save_name}_hurry_up: Triggered when the ball save enters hurry-up state
  • {ball_save_name}_saving_ball: Triggered when a ball is being saved

Replace {ball_save_name} with your actual ball save name (prefixed with "ball_save_" internally).

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, ball saves are configured with: - No active time, grace period, or hurry-up time - No enable, disable, or timer start events - Auto launch disabled - Balls to save set to 1 - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Ball saves are managed within the context of a mode
  • The ball save system automatically handles ball draining and replacement
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track ball save operations
  • The system prevents multiple ball save operations from overlapping
  • Ball saves can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The ball save timer can be started automatically or triggered by specific events
  • Grace period and hurry-up states can be used to provide visual or audio cues to the player

docs.title: Ball search
docs.text: Ball search tries device actions after a period without playfield activity. It relies on correct ball tracking, a configured plunger and working device callbacks. Set those up before enabling it.

docs.title: Enable during configuration
docs.text:
With EnableGlfBallSearch()
    .Timeout = 15000
    .SearchInterval = 150
End With

Call this once before Glf_Init. It creates the search controller and a glf_ball_search mode started by reset_complete. That mode detects a flipper cradle after three seconds, pauses search while the cradle is active and resets it on release.

Setting Default Current behavior Timeout 15000 ms Delay used when resetting or retrying search SearchInterval 150 ms Delay between device attempts BallSearchWaitAfterIteration 10000 ms Exposed setting, but not used by the current search loop Debug False Debug flag; verify logging against the framework revision

The constructor initially schedules a 15-second timeout before these setters run. A custom Timeout applies to subsequent resets/retries, not retroactively to that first scheduled delay.

docs.title: When search runs
docs.text:
The controller checks that a game is running, balls are in play, at least one is not accounted for by ball holds, and the plunger is empty. A failed check schedules another attempt. Normal switch activity participates in resetting search through GLF's event handling.

Search visits autofire devices, ball devices, drop targets and diverters, calling each device's BallSearch(phase) method. It progresses through phases up to 3. The actual action is defined by each device. Flippers, magnets and standup targets are not additional groups in this loop.

The listed device types expose ExcludeFromBallSearch. Set it during device configuration for a mechanism that should not fire during recovery. Diverters also expose BallSearchHoldTime for their search action.

docs.title: Events and recovery
docs.text:
Listen for ball_search_started and ball_search_stopped if a feature needs to release a hold or end a presentation. Dark Chaos's victory-lap mode responds to search by releasing the moon ball and ending the feature. Keep recovery actions compatible with the device's current state.

Test a stationary playfield ball, an occupied plunger, a flipper cradle, a deliberately held scoop ball and every configured search device. Check the table's device arrays too: the current loop only advances to the next group after a device callback; an empty group can prevent traversal from reaching later groups. Do not assume a table with no autofire devices will search every other device.

Source: scripts/src/ball-search.vbs and each participating device's BallSearch implementation. The example table contains a commented-out setup block in _configuration.vbs; it is a reference, not evidence that search is enabled in that table.

docs.title: Combo Switches Configuration
docs.text: The combo switches configuration allows you to set up and customize combinations of switches that trigger events when activated in specific patterns. Combo switches are useful for creating complex gameplay mechanics that require multiple switches to be activated in sequence.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic combo switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ComboSwitches("combo_name")
        .Switch1 = "switch1"              ' First switch in the combo
        .Switch2 = "switch2"              ' Second switch in the combo
        .EventsWhenBoth = Array("event1") ' Events triggered when both switches are active
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced combo switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ComboSwitches("combo_name")
        ' Basic settings
        .Switch1 = "switch1"              ' First switch in the combo
        .Switch2 = "switch2"              ' Second switch in the combo

        ' Timing settings
        .HoldTime = 500                   ' Time in milliseconds a switch must be held to be considered active
        .MaxOffsetTime = 1000             ' Maximum time difference between switch activations to trigger "both" state
        .ReleaseTime = 300                ' Time in milliseconds a switch must be released to be considered inactive

        ' Event settings
        .EventsWhenBoth = Array("event1", "event2")       ' Events triggered when both switches are active
        .EventsWhenInactive = Array("event3", "event4")   ' Events triggered when no switches are active
        .EventsWhenOne = Array("event5", "event6")        ' Events triggered when only one switch is active
        .EventsWhenSwitch1 = Array("event7", "event8")    ' Events triggered when only switch1 is active
        .EventsWhenSwitch2 = Array("event9", "event10")   ' Events triggered when only switch2 is active

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True                     ' Enable debug logging for this combo switch
    End With
End With

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
• Switch1: Name of the first switch in the combo (Default: Empty)
  • Switch2: Name of the second switch in the combo (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Timing Settings
docs.text:
• HoldTime: Time in milliseconds a switch must be held to be considered active (Default: 0)
  • MaxOffsetTime: Maximum time difference between switch activations to trigger "both" state (Default: -1, meaning no limit)
  • ReleaseTime: Time in milliseconds a switch must be released to be considered inactive (Default: 0)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EventsWhenBoth: Array of event names triggered when both switches are active (Default: Empty Array)
  • EventsWhenInactive: Array of event names triggered when no switches are active (Default: Empty Array)
  • EventsWhenOne: Array of event names triggered when only one switch is active (Default: Empty Array)
  • EventsWhenSwitch1: Array of event names triggered when only switch1 is active (Default: Empty Array)
  • EventsWhenSwitch2: Array of event names triggered when only switch2 is active (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this combo switch (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Combo Switch Example
docs.text:
' Basic combo switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ComboSwitches("ramp_combo")
        .Switch1 = "ramp1"
        .Switch2 = "ramp2"
        .EventsWhenBoth = Array("ramp_combo_complete")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Combo Switch Example
docs.text:
' Advanced combo switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ComboSwitches("multiball_combo")
        ' Basic settings
        .Switch1 = "left_ramp"
        .Switch2 = "right_ramp"

        ' Timing settings
        .HoldTime = 300
        .MaxOffsetTime = 2000
        .ReleaseTime = 200

        ' Event settings
        .EventsWhenBoth = Array("multiball_start")
        .EventsWhenInactive = Array("multiball_ended")
        .EventsWhenOne = Array("combo_partial")
        .EventsWhenSwitch1 = Array("left_ramp_complete")
        .EventsWhenSwitch2 = Array("right_ramp_complete")

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: States
docs.text:
The combo switch system manages several states:

  • both: Both switches are active
  • one: Only one switch is active
  • inactive: No switches are active
  • switches_1: Only switch1 is active
  • switches_2: Only switch2 is active

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The combo switch system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • {combo_name}_switch1_active: Triggered when switch1 becomes active
  • {combo_name}_switch1_inactive: Triggered when switch1 becomes inactive
  • {combo_name}_switch2_active: Triggered when switch2 becomes active
  • {combo_name}_switch2_inactive: Triggered when switch2 becomes inactive

Replace {combo_name} with your actual combo switch name (prefixed with "combo_switch_" internally).

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, combo switches are configured with: - No switches defined - No hold time, max offset time, or release time - No events for any state - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Combo switches are managed within the context of a mode
  • The combo switch system automatically handles switch state transitions
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track combo switch operations
  • The system prevents multiple state transitions from overlapping
  • Combo switches can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • Hold time and release time can be used to create more reliable combo detection
  • Max offset time can be used to create time-sensitive combo requirements

docs.title: Configuration: VBScript and YAML
docs.text:
GLF in this repository creates devices and modes through VBScript. It can export MPF YAML from those objects. YAML light shows have a separate conversion workflow that produces VBScript shows for VPX.

What you want to change Where to edit How it reaches the game VPX devices, rules and scoring Table configuration and mode .vbs files Calls to CreateGlfMode, device constructors and their properties MPF configuration exported by GLF The originating GLF configuration Debug export writes glf_mpf/config, glf_mpf/modes and glf_mpf/shows A light animation exported from Godot Show .yaml file Convert to .glf.vbs, then include it in the table script

The current source does not provide a general YAML loader for mode and device configuration. Editing an exported mode YAML file does not change the VPX game. MPF compatibility is a project goal; a ToYaml method alone does not establish identical behavior in both runtimes.

docs.title: Start with a working table
docs.text: Follow installation for the VPX hooks and environment setup for the example table build workflow. In both supplied game projects, look in scripts/src/game/_configuration.vbs and scripts/src/game/modes/ for game configuration. A mode creation sub must be called during configuration before Glf_Init; merely defining the sub does not register the mode.

docs.title: Read a mode alongside its YAML
docs.text:
This reduced example follows Dark Chaos's double-scoring mode. Call CreateDoubleScoringMode from your configuration entry point. Register scoring_multiplier with Glf_SetInitialPlayerVar "scoring_multiplier", 1 during setup, and make scoring expressions use it as shown in dynamic values.

Sub CreateDoubleScoringMode
    With CreateGlfMode("double_scoring", 700)
        .StartEvents = Array("start_double_scoring")
        .StopEvents = Array("mode_base_stopping", "stop_double_scoring")

        With .Timers("double_scoring")
            .TickInterval = 1000
            .StartValue = 0
            .EndValue = 60
            With .ControlEvents()
                .EventName = "mode_double_scoring_started"
                .Action = "restart"
            End With
        End With

        With .EventPlayer()
            .Add "timer_double_scoring_complete", Array("stop_double_scoring")
        End With

        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("mode_double_scoring_started")
                With .Variable("scoring_multiplier")
                    .Action = "set"
                    .Int = 2
                End With
            End With
            With .EventName("mode_double_scoring_stopping")
                With .Variable("scoring_multiplier")
                    .Action = "set"
                    .Int = 1
                End With
            End With
        End With
    End With
End Sub

The corresponding YAML structure is below. This is an MPF configuration excerpt, not a file to load into VPX.

#config_version=6
mode:
  start_events: start_double_scoring
  stop_events: mode_base_stopping, stop_double_scoring
  priority: 700

timers:
  double_scoring:
    start_value: 0
    end_value: 60
    direction: up
    tick_interval: 1000ms
    control_events:
      - event: mode_double_scoring_started
        action: restart

event_player:
  timer_double_scoring_complete:
    - stop_double_scoring

variable_player:
  mode_double_scoring_started:
    scoring_multiplier:
      action: set
      int: 2
  mode_double_scoring_stopping:
    scoring_multiplier:
      action: set
      int: 1

The timer and players are siblings of mode, not nested under it. The timer counts from 0 to 60 with a one-second interval. Completion posts stop_double_scoring; the stopping event restores the multiplier. mode_base_stopping also stops the feature if the base mode ends first.

docs.title: Export and compare
docs.text:
Glf_Init exports MPF configuration when glf_debugEnabled is true. The table's Glf Debug Log option controls that flag through Glf_Options. It must be enabled when initialization runs; changing the option after initialization does not itself run the exporter. Export writes files under the relative glf_mpf directory and can overwrite earlier exports.

Use the runtime implementation to establish behavior, then inspect its ToYaml method to see the exported spelling and units. For example, a timer's .TickInterval = 1000 exports as tick_interval: 1000ms. Do not assume all numeric properties use the same unit: show step times are in seconds.

docs.title: Examples to explore
docs.text:

docs.text: In the GLF repository, scripts/src/_.main.vbs contains Glf_Init, input parsing and export orchestration. The implementations for the example above are scripts/src/commands/mode.vbs, timer.vbs, event-player.vbs and variable-player.vbs. docs.title: Counter
docs.text: A simple counter to monitor things like the number of times a target for switch has been hit.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Dim counter_pop_hits
Set counter_pop_hits = (new Counter)("pop_hits", mode_super_pops)

With counter_pop_hits
    .EnableEvents = Array("mode_super_pops_started")
    .CountEvents = Array("sw30_active", "sw31_active", "sw32_active")
    .CountCompleteValue = 20
    .DisableOnComplete = True
    .ResetOnComplete = True
    .EventsWhenComplete = Arrry("super_pops_qualified")
    .PersistState = True
End With

In the above example we created a counter called counter_pop_hits that belongs to the mode called mode_super_pops. The counter is enabled when the mode starts and will increase its count value whenever one of the three pop bumbers are hit (sw30,sw31,sw32). Once complete, the counter will disable and reset its count and emit the event super_pops_qualified. The Persist State property means the counter will not reset between balls.

docs.title: Name
docs.text:
String

The name of this device. Events emitted from the device will be in the format name_counter

docs.title: Mode
docs.text:
String

This is the mode the counter belongs to.

docs.title: Diverter Configuration
docs.text: The diverter configuration allows you to set up and customize diverters in your pinball machine. Diverters are used to change the path of balls by activating mechanical devices.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
With CreateGlfDiverter("lock_pin")
    .EnableEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .ActivateEvents = Array("raise_lock_pin")
    .DeactivateEvents = Array("drop_lock_pin")
    .ActivationTime = "3000"
    .ActionCallback = "DiverterLockPin"
End With

The Action Callback property needs implementing to actually move the diverter.

Sub DiverterLockPin(enabled)
    If enabled Then
        DiverterPin.isdropped=False
    Else
        DiverterPin.isdropped=True
    End If
End Sub

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text: • ActionCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the diverter activates or deactivates (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EnableEvents: Array of event names that will enable the diverter (Default: Empty Array)
  • DisableEvents: Array of event names that will disable the diverter (Default: Empty Array)
  • ActivateEvents: Array of event names that will activate the diverter (Default: Empty Array)
  • DeactivateEvents: Array of event names that will deactivate the diverter (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Timing Settings
docs.text: • ActivationTime: Integer specifying how long to hold the diverter active in milliseconds (Default: 0)

docs.title: Switch Settings
docs.text: • ActivationSwitches: Array of switch names that will activate the diverter when triggered (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Ball Search Settings
docs.text:
• BallSearchHoldTime: Integer specifying how long to hold the diverter during ball search in milliseconds (Default: 1000)
  • ExcludeFromBallSearch: Boolean indicating whether to exclude this device from ball search operations (Default: False)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this device (Default: False)

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The diverter system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • diverter_{device_name}_activating: Triggered when the diverter is being activated
  • diverter_{device_name}_deactivating: Triggered when the diverter is being deactivated

Replace {device_name} with your actual diverter name.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, diverters are configured with: - No enable/disable events - No activation/deactivation events - No activation switches - Activation time of 0 milliseconds - Ball search hold time of 1000 milliseconds - Debug logging disabled - Not excluded from ball search

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The diverter system automatically manages enable/disable states based on configured events
  • Action callbacks receive a parameter indicating the state (1 for activate, 0 for deactivate)
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track diverter state changes
  • Ball search functionality is available for troubleshooting
  • Diverters can be configured to automatically deactivate after a specified time
  • Activation switches provide direct control without requiring events
  • The system prevents multiple activation/deactivation operations from overlapping

docs.title: DOF Player Configuration
docs.text: The DOF player configuration allows you to set up and customize Direct Output Framework (DOF) events in your pinball machine. DOF players are used to trigger physical feedback effects like solenoids, motors, and other physical outputs.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic DOF player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .DofPlayer
        With .EventName("dof_event")
            .DOFEvent = 123  ' DOF event number
            .Action = "DOF_ON"  ' Action to perform
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced DOF player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .DofPlayer
        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True

        ' Configure DOF events
        With .EventName("flipper_event")
            .DOFEvent = 10
            .Action = "DOF_PULSE"
        End With

        With .EventName("bumper_event")
            .DOFEvent = 20
            .Action = "DOF_ON"
        End With

        With .EventName("motor_event")
            .DOFEvent = 30
            .Action = "DOF_OFF"
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: DOF Event Settings
docs.text:
• DOFEvent: The DOF event number to trigger (Default: Empty)
  • Action: The action to perform on the DOF event (Default: Empty)
  • DOF_OFF: Turn off the output (value: 0)
  • DOF_ON: Turn on the output (value: 1)
  • DOF_PULSE: Pulse the output (value: 2)
  • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this DOF player (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic DOF Player Example
docs.text:
' Basic DOF player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .DofPlayer
        With .EventName("flipper_event")
            .DOFEvent = 10
            .Action = "DOF_PULSE"
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced DOF Player Example
docs.text:
' Advanced DOF player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .DofPlayer
        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True

        ' Configure DOF events
        With .EventName("jackpot_event")
            .DOFEvent = 100
            .Action = "DOF_PULSE"
        End With

        With .EventName("special_event")
            .DOFEvent = 200
            .Action = "DOF_ON"
        End With

        With .EventName("reset_event")
            .DOFEvent = 300
            .Action = "DOF_OFF"
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: DOF Player System
docs.text:
The DOF player system manages physical output events with the following features:

  • DOF events can be configured with different actions (ON, OFF, PULSE)
  • DOF players are managed within the context of a mode
  • Events are triggered when the corresponding event is fired

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The DOF player system responds to events by triggering the configured DOF events with the specified actions.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, DOF players are configured with: - No events defined - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• DOF players are managed within the context of a mode
  • The DOF player system automatically handles event activation and deactivation
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track DOF player operations
  • DOF players can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The DOFEvent property specifies which DOF event to trigger
  • The Action property determines what action to take on the DOF event
  • DOF events are triggered when the corresponding event is fired
  • The system uses the VPX DOF function to trigger physical outputs

docs.title: Drop Target Configuration
docs.text: The drop target configuration allows you to set up and customize drop targets in your pinball machine. Drop targets are interactive targets that can be knocked down and reset, often used in banks or groups.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic drop target configuration
With CreateGlfDropTarget("droptarget_name")
    .Switch = "s_droptarget_switch"       ' Name of the switch that detects when the target is hit
    .Coil = "c_droptarget_coil"           ' Name of the coil to reset the target
    .ActionCallback = "DropTargetAction"  ' Name of the callback function for drop target actions
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced drop target configuration
With CreateGlfDropTarget("droptarget_name")
    ' Basic settings
    .Switch = "s_droptarget_switch"
    .Coil = "c_droptarget_coil"
    .ActionCallback = "DropTargetAction"

    ' Event settings
    .EnableEvents = Array("ball_started")                    ' Events that enable the drop target
    .DisableEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "service_mode")  ' Events that disable the drop target
    .ResetEvents = Array("event1", "event2")                 ' Events that reset the drop target

    ' Ball search settings
    .BallSearchEvents = Array("ball_search_started")         ' Events that trigger ball search
    .BallSearchDelay = 500                                   ' Delay before ball search reset

    ' Debug settings
    .Debug = True                                           ' Enable debug logging for this device
End With

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
• Switch: String name of the switch that detects when the target is hit (Default: Empty)
  • Coil: String name of the coil to reset the target (Default: Empty)
  • ActionCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the drop target is hit or reset (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EnableEvents: Array of event names that will enable the drop target (Default: Array("ball_started"))
  • DisableEvents: Array of event names that will disable the drop target (Default: Array("ball_will_end", "service_mode_entered"))
  • ResetEvents: Array of event names that will reset the drop target (Default: Array("machine_reset_phase_3", "ball_starting"))

docs.title: Ball Search Settings
docs.text:
• BallSearchEvents: Array of event names that will trigger ball search (Default: Array("ball_search_started"))
  • BallSearchDelay: Integer specifying the delay in milliseconds before reset during ball search (Default: 500)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this device (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Drop Target Example
docs.text:
' Basic drop target configuration
With CreateGlfDropTarget("target1")
    .Switch = "s_target1"
    .Coil = "c_target1"
    .ActionCallback = "TargetAction"
End With

docs.title: Advanced Drop Target Example
docs.text:
' Advanced drop target configuration
With CreateGlfDropTarget("bank1")
    .Switch = "s_bank1"
    .Coil = "c_bank1"
    .ActionCallback = "BankAction"
    .EnableEvents = Array("multiball_started")
    .DisableEvents = Array("multiball_ended")
    .ResetEvents = Array("bank_reset")
    .BallSearchEvents = Array("ball_search_started", "ball_search_ended")
    .BallSearchDelay = 750
    .Debug = True
End With

docs.title: Basic Drop Target Callback
docs.text:
' Basic drop target callback
Sub DropTargetAction(State)
    ' Code to handle drop target action
    If State = 1 Then
        ' Drop target is being hit
        PlaySound "target_sound"
    ElseIf State = 0 Then
        ' Drop target is being reset
        PlaySound "reset_sound"
    End If
End Sub

docs.title: Advanced Drop Target Callback
docs.text:
' Advanced drop target callback with additional logic
Sub DropTargetAction(State)
    If State = 1 Then
        ' Drop target is being hit
        PlaySound "target_sound"
        LightOn "l_target_hit"

        ' Add score
        AddScore 1000

        ' Check if all targets are down
        CheckAllTargetsDown
    ElseIf State = 0 Then
        ' Drop target is being reset
        PlaySound "reset_sound"
        LightOff "l_target_hit"
    End If
End Sub

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The drop target system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • {droptarget_name}_hit: Triggered when the drop target is hit
  • {droptarget_name}_resetting: Triggered when the drop target is being reset
  • {droptarget_name}_reset: Triggered when the drop target has been reset
  • {droptarget_name}_enabled: Triggered when the drop target is enabled
  • {droptarget_name}_disabled: Triggered when the drop target is disabled

Replace {droptarget_name} with your actual drop target name (prefixed with "droptarget_" internally).

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, drop targets are configured with: - Enabled on ball_started event - Disabled on ball_will_end and service_mode_entered events - Reset on machine_reset_phase_3 and ball_starting events - Ball search triggered on ball_search_started event - Ball search delay of 500 milliseconds - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The drop target system automatically manages enable/disable states based on configured events
  • Action callbacks receive a parameter indicating the state (1 for hit, 0 for reset)
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track drop target state changes
  • Drop targets can be configured to reset during ball search with a configurable delay
  • The system prevents multiple reset operations from overlapping
  • Drop targets can be used individually or in banks for more complex gameplay

docs.title: Dynamic runtime values
docs.text: Some GLF properties accept expressions evaluated when the value is used. For these properties, pass the expression as a VBScript string. For example, .Int = "100000 * current_player.scoring_multiplier" defers evaluation until the scoring event; removing the quotes attempts to evaluate current_player as a VBScript object during configuration.

docs.title: Score with a multiplier
docs.text:
Initialize your custom variable during table configuration:

Glf_SetInitialPlayerVar "scoring_multiplier", 1

Inside an active mode, configure the scoring event:

With .VariablePlayer()
    With .EventName("jackpot_hit")
        With .Variable("score")
            .Action = "add"
            .Int = "100000 * current_player.scoring_multiplier"
        End With
    End With
End With

A multiplier of 2 awards 200,000 points when jackpot_hit occurs. Dark Chaos uses this pattern in scripts/src/game/modes/score.vbs; the example table constructs similar strings using x & " * current_player.scoring_multiplier".

The exported YAML uses the expression directly:

variable_player:
  jackpot_hit:
    score:
      action: add
      int: 100000 * current_player.scoring_multiplier

See configuration for how exported YAML relates to the VPX source.

docs.title: Runtime references
docs.text:
Reference Reads Requirement current_player.score Current player's score An active player current_player.scoring_multiplier A custom player variable Initialize it during configuration machine.my_variable A machine variable's value Create the machine variable first device.timers.double_scoring.ticks A timer's current count A configured timer named double_scoring device.timers.double_scoring.ticks_remaining A timer's remaining count A configured timer named double_scoring kwargs.amount Data carried by the current event The event must supply amount

Device attributes are limited to those exposed by that device's GetValue implementation; arbitrary VBScript properties are not automatically available as placeholders. The parser also handles players[...], modes and game references; check their implementations before relying on an attribute or index convention.

docs.title: Conditions on events
docs.text:
A condition inside braces filters an event subscription. This pattern from Dark Chaos changes a shot state near the end of a timer:

With .Shots("double_scoring")
    With .ControlEvents()
        .Events = Array("timer_double_scoring_tick{device.timers.double_scoring.ticks == 55}")
        .State = 2
    End With
End With

This excerpt belongs inside the mode containing the timer and requires a shot profile with state index 2. The condition is evaluated when the tick event arrives; it does not continuously watch the timer.

docs.title: Check whether a property supports expressions
docs.text:
In scripts/src/commands/ or scripts/src/devices/, inspect the property's setter. A setter that calls CreateGlfInput supports the runtime input parser. A setter that stores a plain value may behave differently. Variable player Int, Float and String use CreateGlfInput; their values are evaluated in Play.

The implementation is in scripts/src/_.main.vbs: Glf_ParseInput, Glf_ParseEventInput, the Glf_Replace...Attributes helpers and GlfInput.Value. Event conditions and value expressions use different parsing paths, so do not assume every expression syntax works in both.

docs.title: Environment Setup
docs.text: This framework can be used by simply including the script within the VPX script editor. However, we recommend a modern workflow for developing tables that uses Git source control and script separation. This approach makes development faster, less error-prone, and more collaborative.

docs.title: Tools You Will Need
docs.text:
• Git (for version control)
  • VS Code (for editing code)
  • Node.js (for running build scripts)

Note: This guide does not cover installing these tools, as there are many excellent guides available online for each one.

docs.title: VPX Tool
docs.text:
You will also need vpxtool by francisdb (GitHub link). At the time of writing, this workflow uses version 0.13.0 (download here).

Download and install vpxtool, then make sure it is available on your command line by adding it to your system's PATH environment variable.

docs.title: Cloning the Example Table
docs.text:
1. Clone the example table repository: https://github.com/mpcarr/vpx-example-glf

  2. Open the project in VS Code.

  3. Open a terminal in VS Code.

  4. Navigate to the scripts directory: cd scripts

  5. Install the Node.js dependencies: npm install

  6. Rename the project and reset git history: npm run rename-project -- NEW_NAME --git This uses script to rename the example table to your new project name. The optional --git command will reset the git commit history so you have a clean repo for your new project.

  7. Build the VPX file: npm run assemble-vpx This uses vpxtool to build the VPX file from the repository. You sould now have a MyProjectName.vpx file in your local directory.

  8. Start the script watcher: npm run script-watcher This will start a file watcher process that automatically rebuilds the table script used by VPX whenever you make changes. Any edits you make to the scripts will now be automatically updated. To cancel the watch you can press Ctrl+C within the terminal window.

  9. Open the VPX table and press Play!

You are now ready to develop and test your VPX GLF table with a modern, efficient workflow.

docs.title: Event Player Configuration
docs.text: The event player configuration allows you to set up and customize event mapping and playback in your pinball machine. Event players are useful for creating complex event chains where one event can trigger multiple other events, with optional conditions.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic event player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .EventPlayer
        .Add "trigger_event", Array("event1", "event2") ' When trigger_event occurs, play event1 and event2
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced event player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .EventPlayer
        ' Map multiple trigger events to their corresponding response events
        .Add "trigger_event1", Array("response_event1", "response_event2")
        .Add "trigger_event2", Array("response_event3", "response_event4")

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True ' Enable debug logging for this event player
    End With
End With

docs.title: Event Mapping
docs.text:
• Add(key, value): Maps a trigger event to an array of response events
  • key: The trigger event name
  • value: Array of response event names to be played when the trigger event occurs

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this event player (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Event Player Example
docs.text:
' Basic event player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .EventPlayer
        .Add "ramp_complete", Array("ramp_award", "ramp_light")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Event Player Example
docs.text:
' Advanced event player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .EventPlayer
        ' Map multiple trigger events to their corresponding response events
        .Add "left_ramp_complete", Array("left_ramp_award", "left_ramp_light")
        .Add "right_ramp_complete", Array("right_ramp_award", "right_ramp_light")
        .Add "multiball_start", Array("multiball_light", "multiball_sound", "multiball_effect")

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Event Handling
docs.text:
The event player system works by:

  1. Listening for trigger events specified in the configuration
  2. When a trigger event occurs, it plays all the response events associated with that trigger
  3. Events are played in the order they appear in the array
  4. The event player automatically handles event registration and cleanup when the mode is activated or deactivated

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The event player system doesn't generate its own events, but it listens for and responds to events defined in your configuration. When a trigger event occurs, the event player will automatically dispatch all the response events associated with that trigger.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, event players are configured with: - No event mappings - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Event players are managed within the context of a mode
  • The event player system automatically handles event registration and cleanup
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track event player operations
  • Event players can be used to create complex event chains
  • Event players can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The event player system is useful for creating reusable event patterns
  • Event players can be used to simplify complex event handling logic

docs.title: Events and event ordering
docs.text: GLF rules communicate by posting named events. Physical switch events typically use <switch_name>_active and <switch_name>_inactive; devices and modes emit their own names. An event name is not a function call. A mode's players respond only while their listeners are active.

docs.title: Map events inside a mode
docs.text:
With .EventPlayer()
    .Add "s_ramp_active", Array("ramp_award", "ramp_feedback")
    .Add "s_ramp_active{current_player.scoring_multiplier == 2}", Array("double_ramp_feedback")
End With

Replace the switch name and initialize scoring_multiplier before use. The conditional entry is an additional listener, not an else branch: both mappings run when the condition is true. See Event Player and dynamic values.

docs.title: Priorities and conditions
docs.text:
Higher numeric listener priorities run first. Mode players normally add the mode priority to an event-specific suffix: ramp_award.2 listens for ramp_award with a priority offset of 2. A suffix is not part of the dispatched event name. A condition follows in braces, for example ramp_award.2{current_player.score > 100000}.

Use explicit priorities when ordering matters; do not rely on the order of separate player sections. Prefer a separate follow-up event when one operation must happen after another. Avoid circular mappings such as A posting B and B posting A.

docs.title: Three dispatch paths
docs.text:
API Behavior Typical use DispatchPinEvent name, data Adds an ordinary event to the dispatch queue processed by the game timer Switch notifications, scoring, feedback DispatchRelayPinEvent(name, value) Calls listeners synchronously, passing each return value to the next Claiming drained or entering balls DispatchQueuePinEvent name, data Queues an event whose handlers can pause the remaining handlers with wait_for Bonus before ball end, a presentation before continuing

Do not assume an ordinary event's effects have happened immediately after DispatchPinEvent returns. Relay callbacks must return the value for the next listener. Queued callbacks must return the event dictionary, using Set for the object result.

docs.title: Custom listeners
docs.text:
Register a callback during configuration:

AddPinEventListener "feature_award", "my_feature_award", "OnFeatureAward", 100, Null

The callback receives args(0) (registration arguments), args(1) (event data), and, for pin-event dispatch, args(2) (event name).

Function OnFeatureAward(args)
    Dim data
    Set data = args(1)
    SetPlayerState "score", GetPlayerState("score") + data("amount")
    Set OnFeatureAward = data
End Function

Post it only with an active player and the expected dictionary:

Dim awardData
Set awardData = GlfKwargs()
awardData.Add "amount", 10000
DispatchPinEvent "feature_award", awardData

The same event can be consumed by a variable player with .Int = "kwargs.amount". Choose one scoring handler to avoid awarding twice. kwargs is meaningful only when the event supplies that data.

Remove a manually registered listener with its exact event and key:

RemovePinEventListener "feature_award", "my_feature_award"

docs.title: Relay and queued handlers
docs.text:
A minimal scalar relay callback preserves the incoming value:

Function PreserveBallCount(args)
    PreserveBallCount = args(1)
End Function

Ball-management handlers modify that count when they claim a ball. Returning nothing can break downstream accounting; use GLF's ball saves, holds and locks rather than adding another drain handler for a normal rule.

For queued work, prefer Queue Relay Player or a mode with UseWaitQueue, as shown in game lifecycle. Make every wait reachable through a completion or cancellation path.

docs.title: Debug an event
docs.text: Check the emitted name, active mode, condition inputs, listener priority, and whether an earlier handler is waiting. Enable logging as described in Debugging. Core implementation: scripts/src/pin-event-handlers.vbs, the dispatch loop in scripts/src/_.main.vbs, and scripts/src/events.vbs for event parsing objects.

docs.title: Extra Ball Configuration
docs.text: The extra ball configuration allows you to set up and customize extra ball awards in your pinball machine. Extra balls are special rewards that give players additional balls to play with, enhancing gameplay and scoring opportunities.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic extra ball configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ExtraBall("extra_ball_name")
        .AwardEvents = Array("event1") ' Event that triggers the extra ball award
        .MaxPerGame = 3               ' Maximum number of extra balls that can be awarded per game
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced extra ball configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ExtraBall("extra_ball_name")
        ' Award settings
        .AwardEvents = Array("event1", "event2", "event3") ' Multiple events that can trigger the extra ball award

        ' Limit settings
        .MaxPerGame = 5               ' Maximum number of extra balls that can be awarded per game

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True                 ' Enable debug logging for this extra ball
    End With
End With

docs.title: Award Settings
docs.text: • AwardEvents: Array of event names that trigger the extra ball award (Default: Empty Array)

docs.title: Limit Settings
docs.text: • MaxPerGame: Maximum number of extra balls that can be awarded per game (Default: 0, meaning unlimited)

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this extra ball (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Extra Ball Example
docs.text:
' Basic extra ball configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ExtraBall("ramp_extra")
        .AwardEvents = Array("ramp_complete")
        .MaxPerGame = 2
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Extra Ball Example
docs.text:
' Advanced extra ball configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .ExtraBall("multiball_extra")
        ' Award settings
        .AwardEvents = Array("left_ramp_complete", "right_ramp_complete", "center_ramp_complete")

        ' Limit settings
        .MaxPerGame = 3

        ' Debug settings
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Extra Ball Tracking
docs.text: The extra ball system tracks: - The total number of extra balls awarded to the player - The number of extra balls awarded for each specific extra ball configuration

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The extra ball system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • {extra_ball_name}_awarded: Triggered when an extra ball is awarded
  • extra_ball_awarded: Generic event triggered when any extra ball is awarded

Replace {extra_ball_name} with your actual extra ball name (prefixed with "extra_ball_" internally).

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, extra balls are configured with: - No award events - No maximum per game limit (0) - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Extra balls are managed within the context of a mode
  • The extra ball system automatically tracks the number of extra balls awarded
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track extra ball operations
  • Extra balls can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The extra ball system prevents exceeding the maximum per game limit
  • Extra balls are awarded by incrementing the player's "extra_balls" state
  • Extra balls can be awarded through multiple different events

docs.title: Game Logic Devices
docs.text:
A well designed Virtual Pinball table contains many of the real world devices such as scoops, vuks (vertical up kickers), plungers, diverters, drop targets e.t.c. These devices are machine wide devices that need to respond to the ball interacting with them. The classes found in the framework mimic these device behaviours by monitoring and dispatching events which other parts of the system can respond to.

  • Ball Device
  • Diverters
  • Drop Targets

docs.title: Game Logic Commands
docs.text:
To program your game, the framework provides a set of classes to manage the game life-cycle, player state, player score, modes, timers, light shows and manage your DMD or LCD game display.

  • Ball Save
  • Counter
  • Event Player
  • Light Player
  • Mode
  • Multball Locks
  • Multiball
  • Show Player
  • Timer

docs.title: Flipper Configuration
docs.text: The flipper configuration allows you to set up and customize flippers in your pinball machine. Flippers are the primary control mechanism for players to interact with the ball.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic flipper configuration
With CreateGlfFlipper("flipper_name")
    .Switch = "s_flipper_switch"       ' Name of the switch that controls the flipper
    .Coil = "c_flipper_coil"           ' Name of the coil that powers the flipper
    .ActionCallback = "FlipperAction"  ' Name of the callback function for flipper actions
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced flipper configuration
With CreateGlfFlipper("flipper_name")
    ' Basic settings
    .Switch = "s_flipper_switch"
    .Coil = "c_flipper_coil"
    .ActionCallback = "FlipperAction"

    ' Event settings
    .EnableEvents = Array("ball_started")                    ' Events that enable the flipper
    .DisableEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "service_mode")  ' Events that disable the flipper
    .ResetEvents = Array("event1", "event2")                 ' Events that reset the flipper

    ' Debug settings
    .Debug = True                                           ' Enable debug logging for this device
End With

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:
• Switch: String name of the switch that controls the flipper (Default: Empty)
  • Coil: String name of the coil that powers the flipper (Default: Empty)
  • ActionCallback: String name of the callback function that executes when the flipper is activated (Default: Empty)

docs.title: Event Control
docs.text:
• EnableEvents: Array of event names that will enable the flipper (Default: Array("ball_started"))
  • DisableEvents: Array of event names that will disable the flipper (Default: Array("ball_will_end", "service_mode_entered"))
  • ResetEvents: Array of event names that will reset the flipper (Default: Array("machine_reset_phase_3", "ball_starting"))

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this device (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Flipper Example
docs.text:
' Basic flipper configuration
With CreateGlfFlipper("left")
    .Switch = "s_left_flipper"
    .Coil = "c_left_flipper"
    .ActionCallback = "LeftFlipperAction"
End With

docs.title: Advanced Flipper Example
docs.text:
' Advanced flipper configuration
With CreateGlfFlipper("right")
    .Switch = "s_right_flipper"
    .Coil = "c_right_flipper"
    .ActionCallback = "RightFlipperAction"
    .EnableEvents = Array("multiball_started")
    .DisableEvents = Array("multiball_ended")
    .ResetEvents = Array("flipper_reset")
    .Debug = True
End With

docs.title: Basic Flipper Callback
docs.text:
' Basic flipper callback
Sub FlipperAction(Enabled)
    ' Code to handle flipper action
    If Enabled Then
        ' Flipper is being activated
        PlaySound "flipper_up"
    Else
        ' Flipper is being deactivated
        PlaySound "flipper_down"
    End If
End Sub

docs.title: Advanced Flipper Callback
docs.text:
' Advanced flipper callback with additional logic
Sub FlipperAction(Enabled)
    If Enabled Then
        ' Flipper is being activated
        PlaySound "flipper_up"
        LightOn "l_flipper_active"

        ' Add score
        AddScore 100
    Else
        ' Flipper is being deactivated
        PlaySound "flipper_down"
        LightOff "l_flipper_active"
    End If
End Sub

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The flipper system generates several events that you can listen to:

  • {flipper_name}_activated: Triggered when the flipper is activated
  • {flipper_name}_deactivated: Triggered when the flipper is deactivated
  • {flipper_name}_enabled: Triggered when the flipper is enabled
  • {flipper_name}_disabled: Triggered when the flipper is disabled

Replace {flipper_name} with your actual flipper name (prefixed with "flipper_" internally).

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, flippers are configured with: - Enabled on ball_started event - Disabled on ball_will_end and service_mode_entered events - Reset on machine_reset_phase_3 and ball_starting events - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The flipper system automatically manages enable/disable states based on configured events
  • Action callbacks receive a parameter indicating the state (1 for activate, 0 for deactivate)
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track flipper state changes
  • Flippers can be configured to activate during specific game modes
  • The system prevents multiple activation/deactivation operations from overlapping

docs.title: Getting started with GLF
docs.text: Start with a working table, then add one rule at a time. GLF's VPX runtime is configured in VBScript; exported MPF YAML is useful for comparison but is not a general configuration input to VPX. See Configuration and YAML.

docs.title: Choose your starting point
docs.text:
To build a game from an empty VPX table, follow Build Your First GLF Game. It includes the object checklist, a cumulative script and a complete-game checkpoint. To start from the supplied example table instead, follow Environment Setup. Keep its working trough, plunger, switch wiring and table hooks while learning the rules system. For an existing VPX table, follow Installation, including the collections, timer and initialization, exit, key and option hooks.

The example table keeps game setup in scripts/src/game/_configuration.vbs, modes in scripts/src/game/modes/, and its bundled framework in scripts/src/glf/glf.vbs. The GLF repository's editable framework source is under scripts/src/; the game may bundle a different revision.

docs.title: First playable rule
docs.text:
1. Verify that a game starts, serves a ball and advances correctly after a drain. Use the trough and plunger tutorials if needed.
  2. Choose an existing switch and confirm its <switch_name>_active event. Use the exact name from the table.
  3. Add a small mode that starts on ball_started, stops on ball_will_end, and awards points with a variable player. Call its creation sub during configuration before Glf_Init.
  4. Rebuild the table script and restart play. Confirm one hit awards points once, including for a second player.
  5. Add feedback with a light player, show or sound.

Follow the complete mode walkthrough when you are ready to add qualification and a timed objective.

docs.title: Suggested reading order
docs.text:
Learn Guide When to start, reset and stop rules Game and ball lifecycle How rules communicate Events Who owns progress and scores Player state and persistence How components form a feature Complete game mode How to add more balls Multiball walkthrough How to present the rules Displays and Godot, sound setup How to investigate a failure Debugging

Examples in these guides either identify their required table objects or use game-defined events. Rename those placeholders to your table's names before use. The guides describe the checked-in implementation; verify changes in VPX as well as reviewing the generated script.

docs.title: High Score Configuration
docs.text: The high score configuration allows you to set up and customize high score tracking in your game. High scores are used to track and display player scores across multiple games.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
Within your ConfigureGlfDevices function, you need to enable highscores. You can create different categories and defaults. Initial values are set first time the game runs. After that, values are read from the machines ini file.

    With EnableGlfHighScores()
        With .Categories()
            .Add "score", Array("GRAND CHAMPION", "HIGH SCORE 1", "HIGH SCORE 2", "HIGH SCORE 3") 
        End With
        With .Defaults("score")
            .Add "DAN", 9000000
            .Add "MPC", 7000000
            .Add "AVE", 5000000
            .Add "DIG", 3000000
        End With
        .EnterInitialsTimeout = 65000
    End With

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install and use the Game Logic Framework in your VPX table, you will need to download the latest vpx-glf.vbs script and include it in your table script

vpx-glf.vbs

docs.title: Global Script Required Settings
docs.text: The GLF requires a few global settings to function correctly.

docs.title: GLF Game Timer
docs.text: Add a timer object to your vpx table called Glf_GameTimer. Set it to Enabled with an Interval of -1ms.

docs.title: GLF Table Collection
docs.text:
Create the following collections using the vpx collections manager (F8).

glf_lights
glf_switches
glf_slingshots
glf_spinners

docs.title: Global Script Settings
docs.text:
• cGameName must be set to your table name
  • BallSize, BallMass, tnob, lob and gBot must be set
  • tablewidth and tableheight must be set.

Example 

Const cGameName = "MyAwesomeGame"
Const BallSize = 50         'Ball diameter in VPX units; must be 50
Const BallMass = 1          'Ball mass must be 1
Const tnob = 6              'Total playable balls (Balls in Trough)
Const lob = 2               'Total non playable balls (Captive Balls)
Dim gBot                    'Collection used for ball tracking
Dim tablewidth: tablewidth = Table1.width
Dim tableheight: tableheight = Table1.height

docs.title: Configure Devices
docs.text:
You'll need an entry point to configure your devices and enable modes. Create a sub called ConfigureGlfDevices

Sub ConfigureGlfDevices
    'Device confguration goes here.
End Sub

docs.title: Adding Hooks into GLF
docs.text: You need to add these calls into to your table event subs.

docs.title: Table Init
docs.text:
Inside Table1_Init add your ConfigureGlfDevices sub call and Glf_Init(Table1)

Example

Sub Table1_Init()
    ConfigureGlfDevices()
    Glf_Init(Table1)
End Sub

docs.title: Table Exit
docs.text:
Inside Table1_Exit add Glf_Exit()

Example

Sub Table1_Exit()
    Glf_Exit()
End Sub

docs.title: Table Keys
docs.text:
Inside your Table1_KeyDown and Sub Table1_KeyUp Subs, add the Glf_KeyDown and Glf_KeyUp calls.

Example

Sub Table1_KeyDown(ByVal keycode)
    Glf_KeyDown(keycode)
End Sub

Sub Table1_KeyUp(ByVal keycode)
    Glf_KeyUp(keycode)
End Sub

docs.title: Table Options
docs.text:
Inside Table1_Options add Glf_Options(eventId)

Example

Sub Table1_OptionEvent(ByVal eventId)
    If eventId = 1 Then DisableStaticPreRendering = True

    Glf_Options(eventId)

    If eventId = 3 Then DisableStaticPreRendering = False
End Sub

docs.title: VPX Light Controller
docs.text:
This page describes the standalone lightController.vbs API. For GLF table setup, use installation, Light Player and light shows.

A class to help vpx original table authors manage light states and custom sequences. Supports managing multiple light states per light, RGB lights, Syncing with VPX light sequences, custom key frame light sequences, import / export of light sequences to show creator and several utility functions for interacting with lights.

docs.title: Installing
docs.text: • Download the latest release from github releases and copy the vbs code from lightController.vbs into your vpx table script.

docs.title: vpmMapLights - what is it?
docs.text:
-vpmMapLights is a function which is available from the core.vbs script that comes with VPX. It allows you to setup your lights by specifying a light index in the lights timer interval property. This means you could have multiple light objects assigned to the same index to generate a greater light influence, or you might want to tie multiple lights together so they flash at the same time. This technique is used in vpx rom based tables to map the lights to the rom index. We use the same setup here for consistency.

  • The first thing you need to do is assign a number to each light or light groups and put that in the light objects timer interval

  • Next you need to add all of your lights into a vpx collection called aLights

  • At the top of your table script, make sure these variables are defined:

Const cGameName = "REPLACE WITH TABLE NAME"
Dim tablewidth: tablewidth = Table1.width
Dim tableheight: tableheight = Table1.height
  • In your table init sub, you can call the light controller's register lights function
lightCtrl.RegisterLights

This will do a few things. First, it will call vpmMapLights to setup your light indexes. Next it will build a grid containing all of your light positions, this is used if you want to export your lights and also for some custom color fading routines. Second, it will try to find any lightmaps that might be assoiciated with your lights. (these are primitives you can setup that need to track the opacity and color of your lights). Finally it will create a Sequence Runner for each light, this allows for each light to have multiple states, e.g. a mode shot and a multiball jackpot shot. More on Sequence Runners below.

  • Finally you need to call lightCtrl.Update() inside a timer. You can reuse an existing timer or setup a new one. A 16ms timer works well

• Managing Lights
