The sound player system manages sound playback with the following features:

  • Sounds can be played in response to events
  • Sounds can be stopped in response to events
  • Sounds can be configured with volume and loop settings
  • Sounds can be identified by keys for stopping
  • Sound players are managed within the context of a mode

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The sound player system doesn't generate its own events, but it responds to events defined in your configuration.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, sound players are configured with: - No events defined - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Sound players are managed within the context of a mode
  • The sound player system automatically handles sound playback
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track sound player operations
  • Sound players can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The sound player system prevents sound conflicts
  • Sounds must be defined in the sound system before they can be played
  • The Action property determines whether a sound is played or stopped
  • The Key property is used to identify sounds for stopping
  • The Volume property can be used to adjust the volume of sounds
  • The Loops property can be used to make sounds loop
  • When a mode is deactivated, all sounds played by that mode are stopped

docs.title: Sound setup and buses
docs.text: Register sounds and buses before configuring the modes that play them. A bus groups sounds and sets default volume and simultaneous-play limits. The sound player maps rule events to those registered sounds.

docs.title: Register a VPX sound
docs.text:
Import a sound into the VPX Sound Manager under the name sfx_award, then configure:

With CreateGlfSoundBus("effects")
    .SimultaneousSounds = 8
    .Volume = 0.5
End With

With CreateGlfSound("award")
    .File = "sfx_award"
    .Bus = "effects"
    .Duration = 1200
    .Loops = 0
    .EventsWhenStopped = Array("award_sound_finished")
End With

Replace Duration with the actual clip length in milliseconds. The local bus schedules bookkeeping and stopped events using that value; it does not obtain the clip length from VPX. A zero duration can therefore signal completion immediately.

Within a mode, play and stop the registered sound:

With .SoundPlayer()
    With .EventName("play_award")
        .Key = "award_audio"
        .Sound = "award"
    End With
    With .EventName("stop_award")
        .Key = "award_audio"
        .Sound = "award"
        .Action = "stop"
    End With
End With

Sound is the GLF registration name; File is the VPX sound name. Keep both the sound and playback key consistent when stopping it.

docs.title: Bus and sound reference
docs.text:
Object/property Default Meaning Bus SimultaneousSounds 8 Limit for distinct locally tracked sound files Bus Volume 0.5 Used when neither sound nor playback entry overrides volume Bus SystemType Empty Local VPX playback; "bcp" delegates to the media controller Sound File, Bus Empty Required asset and bus names Sound Volume Empty Overrides the bus volume when set Sound Duration 0 Local completion scheduling in milliseconds Sound Loops 0 Passed to local VPX playback; use 0 for a single play Sound EventsWhenStopped Empty Events emitted when the bus stops that sound Sound Priority 0 Stored/exported; local playback does not use it to preempt sounds Sound MaxQueueTime -1 Stored/exported; local queuing is not implemented

Playback-entry volume overrides sound volume, which overrides bus volume. These values replace one another rather than multiplying together. Use separate music, effects and voice buses for independently configured defaults, as the example table does in _configuration.vbs.

The local bus tracks by sound file. Replaying the same file replaces its tracked entry and stop timer; it does not create independent instances just because playback keys differ. At capacity, the local bus's queue branch is a TODO, so do not rely on excess sounds being played later or high-priority sounds evicting lower-priority ones.

docs.title: Music and BCP audio
docs.text:
For repeating music, configure the sound's loop behavior and an explicit stop event when the feature ends. Test loop duration and completion behavior separately from one-shot clips. Do not use show-player loop semantics as sound-player documentation: these are different implementations.

A bus with .SystemType = "bcp" sends sound play/stop commands only when BCP is enabled. The media project must define the corresponding GLF sound name. The BCP path does not apply the same local duration/volume/queue logic; configure media-side playback accordingly. See Displays and Godot.

Verify sound names, duration, repeated triggers, bus saturation, mode cleanup and the stopped event before using sound completion to advance a rule. Working examples: the example table's scripts/src/game/modes/sounds.vbs and _configuration.vbs; source: scripts/src/devices/sound-system.vbs and commands/sound-player.vbs.

docs.title: Standup targets
docs.text: Register a standup target so GLF can generate its hit/unhit wiring and emit switch events. This is a global device configured before Glf_Init, not a mode component.

docs.title: Basic target
docs.text:
The table must contain a target object named s_ST1:

With CreateGlfStanduptarget("target1")
    .Switch = "s_ST1"
End With

GLF generates the target's event subs. Do not also add it to glf_switches or duplicate its _Hit/_UnHit subs; the example table explicitly keeps standup targets out of those collections.

For a non-Roth target, generated hit/unhit handlers post s_ST1_active and s_ST1_inactive while the game is not tilted. Listen for the active event in a shot or event player; registration itself does not award points.

docs.title: Roth target integration
docs.text:
If the table already has working Roth standup physics and its associated STHit implementation:

With CreateGlfStanduptarget("target1")
    .Switch = "s_ST1"
    .UseRothStanduptarget = True
    .RothSTSwitchID = 1
End With

The ID must match the table's Roth configuration. GLF's generated hit handler calls STHit instead of directly posting the switch event. The physics integration must emit the GLF events at the appropriate target action; inspect the example table's scripts/src/vpx/standup-targets.vbs alongside _configuration.vbs.

Property Default Purpose Switch Empty VPX target object name UseRothStanduptarget False Route hits through Roth target physics RothSTSwitchID -1 ID passed to STHit Debug False Device logging flag

Test one physical hit produces one rule hit, including after a tilt and on the next ball. Related: shots, drop targets. Source: scripts/src/devices/standup-target.vbs and handler generation in scripts/src/_.main.vbs.

docs.title: State Machine Configuration
docs.text: The state machine configuration allows you to set up and customize state-based behavior in your pinball machine. State machines are used to manage complex game logic with multiple states and transitions.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic state machine configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .StateMachine("state_machine_name")
        ' Configure starting state
        .StartingState = "idle"

        ' Configure states
        With .States("idle")
            .Label = "Idle State"
        End With

        With .States("active")
            .Label = "Active State"
        End With

        ' Configure transitions
        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("idle")
            .Target = "active"
            .Events = Array("start_event")
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced state machine configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .StateMachine("state_machine_name")
        ' Configure persistence
        .PersistState = True

        ' Configure starting state
        .StartingState = "idle"

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True

        ' Configure states
        With .States("idle")
            .Label = "Idle State"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("idle_state_started")
            .EventsWhenStopped = Array("idle_state_stopped")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "idle_show"
                .Loops = 1
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        With .States("active")
            .Label = "Active State"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("active_state_started")
            .EventsWhenStopped = Array("active_state_stopped")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "active_show"
                .Loops = 0
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        With .States("complete")
            .Label = "Complete State"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("complete_state_started")
            .EventsWhenStopped = Array("complete_state_stopped")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "complete_show"
                .Loops = 1
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        ' Configure transitions
        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("idle")
            .Target = "active"
            .Events = Array("start_event")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("transitioning_to_active")
        End With

        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("active")
            .Target = "complete"
            .Events = Array("complete_event")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("transitioning_to_complete")
        End With

        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("complete")
            .Target = "idle"
            .Events = Array("reset_event")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("transitioning_to_idle")
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: State Machine Settings
docs.text:
• StartingState: The state to start in when the state machine is activated (Default: "start")
  • PersistState: Whether to persist the state between balls (Default: False)
  • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this state machine (Default: False)

docs.title: State Settings
docs.text:
• Label: A human-readable label for the state
  • EventsWhenStarted: Array of events to fire when the state starts
  • EventsWhenStopped: Array of events to fire when the state stops
  • ShowWhenActive: Show to play when the state is active
  • InternalCacheId: Internal cache ID for the state

docs.title: Transition Settings
docs.text:
• Source: Array of source states that can transition to the target state
  • Target: The target state to transition to
  • Events: Array of events that trigger the transition
  • EventsWhenTransitioning: Array of events to fire when transitioning

docs.title: Basic State Machine Example
docs.text:
' Basic state machine configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .StateMachine("ramp_state")
        ' Configure starting state
        .StartingState = "idle"

        ' Configure states
        With .States("idle")
            .Label = "Idle State"
        End With

        With .States("active")
            .Label = "Active State"
        End With

        ' Configure transitions
        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("idle")
            .Target = "active"
            .Events = Array("ramp_enter")
        End With

        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("active")
            .Target = "idle"
            .Events = Array("ramp_exit")
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced State Machine Example
docs.text:
' Advanced state machine configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .StateMachine("jackpot_state")
        ' Configure persistence
        .PersistState = True

        ' Configure starting state
        .StartingState = "idle"

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True

        ' Configure states
        With .States("idle")
            .Label = "Idle State"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("jackpot_idle")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "jackpot_idle_show"
                .Loops = 1
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        With .States("collecting")
            .Label = "Collecting Jackpot"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("jackpot_collecting")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "jackpot_collecting_show"
                .Loops = 0
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        With .States("complete")
            .Label = "Jackpot Complete"
            .EventsWhenStarted = Array("jackpot_complete")
            With .ShowWhenActive
                .Show = "jackpot_complete_show"
                .Loops = 1
                .Speed = 1.0
            End With
        End With

        ' Configure transitions
        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("idle")
            .Target = "collecting"
            .Events = Array("jackpot_start")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("starting_jackpot")
        End With

        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("collecting")
            .Target = "complete"
            .Events = Array("jackpot_collected")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("completing_jackpot")
        End With

        With .Transitions
            .Source = Array("complete")
            .Target = "idle"
            .Events = Array("jackpot_reset")
            .EventsWhenTransitioning = Array("resetting_jackpot")
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: State Machine System
docs.text:
The state machine system manages state-based behavior with the following features:

  • States can be defined with labels, events, and shows
  • Transitions can be defined between states
  • States can fire events when started or stopped
  • Transitions can fire events when transitioning
  • Shows can be played when a state is active
  • State machines can persist their state between balls
  • State machines are managed within the context of a mode

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The state machine system generates the following events:

  • Events defined in EventsWhenStarted when a state starts
  • Events defined in EventsWhenStopped when a state stops
  • Events defined in EventsWhenTransitioning when transitioning between states

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, state machines are configured with: - Starting state of "start" - No persistence between balls - No states defined - No transitions defined - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• State machines are managed within the context of a mode
  • The state machine system automatically handles state transitions
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track state machine operations
  • State machines can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The state machine system prevents state conflicts
  • State persistence is useful for maintaining state between balls
  • Shows can be used to provide visual feedback for the current state
  • Events can be used to trigger actions when states change
  • Transitions can be triggered by multiple events
  • Multiple source states can transition to the same target state

docs.title: Tilt Configuration
docs.text: The tilt configuration allows you to set up and customize tilt behavior in your pinball machine. The tilt system manages tilt warnings, tilt events, and slam tilts.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic tilt configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .Tilt
        .WarningsToTilt = 3
        .SettleTime = 5000  ' 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) settle time
        .MultipleHitWindow = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) multiple hit window
        .ResetWarningEvents = Array("reset_warnings_event")
        .TiltWarningEvents = Array("tilt_warning_event")
        .TiltEvents = Array("tilt_event")
        .TiltSlamTiltEvents = Array("slam_tilt_event")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced tilt configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .Tilt
        ' Configure tilt settings
        .WarningsToTilt = 3
        .SettleTime = 5000  ' 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) settle time
        .MultipleHitWindow = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) multiple hit window

        ' Configure events
        .ResetWarningEvents = Array("reset_warnings_event1", "reset_warnings_event2")
        .TiltWarningEvents = Array("tilt_warning_event1", "tilt_warning_event2")
        .TiltEvents = Array("tilt_event1", "tilt_event2")
        .TiltSlamTiltEvents = Array("slam_tilt_event1", "slam_tilt_event2")

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Tilt Settings
docs.text:
• WarningsToTilt: Number of warnings before a tilt occurs (Default: 0)
  • SettleTime: Time in milliseconds to wait before clearing a tilt (Default: 0)
  • MultipleHitWindow: Time window in milliseconds for multiple hits to count as one warning (Default: 0)
  • ResetWarningEvents: Array of events that reset the tilt warnings
  • TiltWarningEvents: Array of events that trigger a tilt warning
  • TiltEvents: Array of events that trigger a tilt
  • TiltSlamTiltEvents: Array of events that trigger a slam tilt
  • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this tilt system (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Tilt Example
docs.text:
' Basic tilt configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .Tilt
        .WarningsToTilt = 3
        .SettleTime = 5000  ' 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) settle time
        .MultipleHitWindow = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) multiple hit window
        .ResetWarningEvents = Array("reset_warnings")
        .TiltWarningEvents = Array("tilt_warning")
        .TiltEvents = Array("tilt")
        .TiltSlamTiltEvents = Array("slam_tilt")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Tilt Example
docs.text:
' Advanced tilt configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .Tilt
        ' Configure tilt settings
        .WarningsToTilt = 3
        .SettleTime = 5000  ' 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) settle time
        .MultipleHitWindow = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) multiple hit window

        ' Configure events
        .ResetWarningEvents = Array("reset_warnings", "ball_started")
        .TiltWarningEvents = Array("tilt_warning_switch", "tilt_warning_event")
        .TiltEvents = Array("tilt_switch", "tilt_event")
        .TiltSlamTiltEvents = Array("slam_tilt_switch", "slam_tilt_event")

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Tilt System
docs.text:
The tilt system manages tilt behavior with the following features:

  • Tilt warnings can be configured with a specific count before a tilt occurs
  • Tilt warnings can be reset by specific events
  • Tilt events can be triggered by specific events
  • Slam tilt events can be triggered by specific events
  • The system tracks the number of tilt warnings for each player
  • The system manages the tilt settle time
  • The system prevents multiple tilt warnings within a short time window
  • The tilt system is managed within the context of a mode

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The tilt system generates the following events:

  • tilt_warning: Fired when a tilt warning occurs
  • tilt_warning_X: Fired when the Xth tilt warning occurs
  • tilt: Fired when a tilt occurs
  • slam_tilt: Fired when a slam tilt occurs
  • tilt_clear: Fired when a tilt is cleared

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, the tilt system is configured with: - No warnings to tilt (WarningsToTilt = 0) - No settle time (SettleTime = 0) - No multiple hit window (MultipleHitWindow = 0) - No reset warning events - No tilt warning events - No tilt events - No slam tilt events - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The tilt system is managed within the context of a mode
  • The tilt system automatically handles tilt warnings and tilts
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track tilt operations
  • The tilt system can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The tilt system prevents tilt conflicts
  • Tilt warnings are tracked per player
  • Tilt warnings are reset when a new ball starts
  • The settle time is used to prevent immediate re-tilting
  • The multiple hit window prevents rapid-fire tilt warnings
  • When a tilt occurs, the current ball ends and all balls drain
  • When all balls have drained, the tilt is cleared after the settle time

docs.title: Timed Switches Configuration
docs.text: The timed switches configuration allows you to set up and customize switches that activate after a specified delay in your pinball machine. Timed switches are useful for creating delayed reactions to switch hits.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic timed switches configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .TimedSwitches("timed_switch_name")
        .Time = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) delay
        .Switches = Array("sw01", "sw02")
        .EventsWhenActive = Array("timed_switch_active")
        .EventsWhenReleased = Array("timed_switch_released")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
' Advanced timed switches configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .TimedSwitches("timed_switch_name")
        ' Configure delay time
        .Time = 2000  ' 2000 milliseconds (2 seconds) delay

        ' Configure switches to monitor
        .Switches = Array("sw01", "sw02", "sw03")

        ' Configure events
        .EventsWhenActive = Array("timed_switch_active", "multiball_start")
        .EventsWhenReleased = Array("timed_switch_released", "multiball_end")

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Timed Switch Settings
docs.text:
• Time: The delay in milliseconds before a switch is considered active (Default: 0)
  • Switches: Array of switch names to monitor
  • EventsWhenActive: Array of events to fire when any of the switches become active
  • EventsWhenReleased: Array of events to fire when all switches are released
  • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this timed switch (Default: False)

docs.title: Basic Timed Switch Example
docs.text:
' Basic timed switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("base", 10)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .TimedSwitches("ramp_switch")
        .Time = 1000  ' 1000 milliseconds (1 second) delay
        .Switches = Array("sw_ramp")
        .EventsWhenActive = Array("ramp_active")
        .EventsWhenReleased = Array("ramp_released")
    End With
End With

docs.title: Advanced Timed Switch Example
docs.text:
' Advanced timed switch configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("multiball", 20)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .TimedSwitches("jackpot_switch")
        ' Configure delay time
        .Time = 2000  ' 2000 milliseconds (2 seconds) delay

        ' Configure switches to monitor
        .Switches = Array("sw_jackpot1", "sw_jackpot2", "sw_jackpot3")

        ' Configure events
        .EventsWhenActive = Array("jackpot_active", "jackpot_ready")
        .EventsWhenReleased = Array("jackpot_released", "jackpot_reset")

        ' Configure debug
        .Debug = True
    End With
End With

docs.title: Timed Switch System
docs.text:
The timed switch system manages delayed switch activation with the following features:

  • Switches can be configured to activate after a specified delay
  • Multiple switches can be monitored simultaneously
  • Events can be fired when switches become active or are released
  • The system tracks which switches are currently active
  • Timed switches are managed within the context of a mode

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
The timed switch system generates the following events:

  • Events defined in EventsWhenActive when any of the switches become active
  • Events defined in EventsWhenReleased when all switches are released

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, timed switches are configured with: - No delay (Time = 0) - No switches to monitor - No events when active or released - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Timed switches are managed within the context of a mode
  • The timed switch system automatically handles switch activation and release
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track timed switch operations
  • Timed switches can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • The timed switch system prevents switch conflicts
  • The delay is applied to each switch individually
  • A switch is considered active only after the delay has passed
  • All switches must be released before the release events are fired
  • The system automatically removes any pending delays when a switch is released

docs.title: Timer Configuration
docs.text: The timer configuration allows you to set up and customize countdown or count-up timers. Timers are useful for creating time-limited modes, bonus rounds, and other time-based events.

docs.title: Configuration Overview
docs.text: Timers are always managed within the context of a mode. The mode itself is responsible for starting and stopping, and you can configure the timer to start running automatically or control it via events and control actions.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic timer configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .Timer("timer_name")
        .StartRunning = True        ' Start timer automatically when mode starts
        .Direction = "down"         ' Count down
        .StartValue = 10            ' Start at 10
        .EndValue = 0               ' End at 0
        .TickInterval = 1000        ' Tick every 1 second
    End With
End With

docs.title: Controlling the Timer with Events
docs.text:
You can control the timer dynamically using control events. For example, you can add time, pause, or change the tick interval:


' Example event player to dispatch custom events.
With .EventPlayer
    .Add("s_switch01_active", Array("add_ticks_to_my_timer")
    .Add("s_switch02_active", Array("pause_my_timer")
End With

With .Timer("timer_name")
    With .ControlEvents
        .EventName = "add_ticks_to_my_timer"
        .Action = "add"
        .Value = 5   ' Add 5 ticks,
    End With
    With .ControlEvents
        .EventName = "pause_my_timer"
        .Action = "pause"
        .Value = 2000   ' Pause for 2 seconds
    End With
End With

docs.title: StartRunning:
docs.text:
type: boolean (True/False). Default: False

Controls whether this timer starts running, or whether it needs to be started with one of the start control events.

docs.title: Direction:
docs.text:
type: string (up/down). Default: up

Controls which direction this timer runs in. Options are up or down.

docs.title: start_value:
docs.text:
Single value, type: integer or template (Instructions for entering templates). Defaults to 0.

The initial value of the timer. When a timer is restarted, this is the value it will always start from. If you ever need to change the value, you can use a jump control action to set it to whatever value you want.

docs.title: end_value:
docs.text:
Single value, type: integer or template (Instructions for entering templates). Defaults to empty.

Specifies what the final value for this timer will be. When the timer value equals or exceeds this (for timers counting up), or when it equals or is lower than this (for timers counting down), the timer_(name)_complete event is posted and the timer is stopped. (If the restart_on_complete: setting is true, then the timer is also reset back to its start_value: and started again.)

docs.title: tick_interval:
docs.text: Single value, type: integer (milliseconds)

docs.title: Control Events
docs.text: • ControlEvents: Configure actions (add, subtract, jump, start, stop, reset, restart,pause, set_tick_internal, change_tick_interval, reset_tick_interval) that can be triggered by events

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this timer (Default: False)

docs.title: Timer Events
docs.text:
The timer system generates the following events

  • timer_NAME_started: Fired when the timer starts
  • timer_NAME_stopped: Fired when the timer stops
  • timer_NAME_complete: Fired when the timer reaches its end value
  • timer_NAME_tick: Fired on each timer tick

docs.title: Variable Player Configuration
docs.text: The variable player configuration allows you to set up and customize variable manipulation in your game. Variable players are used to modify player and machine variables based on events.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
' Basic variable player configuration within a mode
With CreateGlfMode("mode_name", priority)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_ended")

    With .VariablePlayer
        With .EventName("event_name")
            With .Variable("variable_name")
                .Action = "add"
                .Int = 100
            End With
        End With
    End With
End With

docs.title: Variable Actions
docs.text:
• Action: Action to perform on the variable
  • add: Add a value to a player variable
  • add_machine: Add a value to a machine variable
  • set: Set a player variable to a specific value
  • set_machine: Set a machine variable to a specific value

docs.title: Variable Types
docs.text:
• Int: Integer value
  • Float: Floating-point value
  • String: String value

docs.title: Debug Settings
docs.text: • Debug: Boolean to enable debug logging for this variable player (Default: False)

docs.title: Machine Variables
docs.text:
Machine variables are persistent across games and can be created using the CreateMachineVar function:

' Create a machine variable
Dim high_score
Set high_score = CreateMachineVar("high_score")
high_score.InitialValue = 0
high_score.Persist = True
high_score.ValueType = "int"

docs.title: Variable Player System
docs.text:
The variable player system manages variable manipulation with the following features:

  • Variables can be modified based on events
  • Both player and machine variables can be manipulated
  • Variables can be added to or set to specific values
  • Variables are managed within the context of a mode

docs.title: Events
docs.text: The variable player system doesn't generate its own events, but it responds to events defined in your configuration.

docs.title: Default Behavior
docs.text: By default, variable players are configured with: - No events defined - Debug logging disabled

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Variable players are managed within the context of a mode
  • The variable player system automatically handles variable manipulation
  • Debug logging can be enabled to track variable player operations
  • Variable players can be configured to work with specific game modes or features
  • Multiple active variable players can respond to the same event; avoid awarding the same score in more than one mode unintentionally
  • Player variables are reset when a new game starts
  • Machine variables persist across games if the Persist property is set to True
  • The add action is useful for incrementing scores or counters
  • The set action is useful for resetting or initializing variables

docs.title: Expressions and YAML
docs.text: Pass runtime expressions as strings, for example .Int = "1000 * current_player.scoring_multiplier". See dynamic values for initialization and examples, and Configuration and YAML for a complete mode with its exported representation.

docs.title: Widget player
docs.text: The widget player sends a named widget to the BCP media controller when an event occurs in an active mode. The widget must already exist in the media project. See Displays and Godot for connection setup.

docs.title: Show an overlay
docs.text:
The example table uses a left_spinner widget in godot/GMCDisplay:

With .WidgetPlayer()
    With .EventName("light_right_orbit")
        .Widget = "left_spinner"
        .Priority = 10
        .Expire = 4
    End With
End With

Place this inside a mode and post light_right_orbit while it is active. Expire is in seconds, unlike segment display player expiry, which is in milliseconds.

Property Default Behavior Widget Empty Name of the media resource to play Priority 0 Offset added to the mode's priority Expire Empty Sent as null when omitted; otherwise passed to media playback Action "play" Stored and exported, but not used by the current runtime playback path Debug False Player debug flag

docs.title: Current runtime limits
docs.text:
Playback requires useBcp = True. The implementation calls bcpController.PlayWidget, which always sends action play and position x=0, y=0. Setting .Action = "remove" does not currently remove a widget through this path. There are no widget-player position or token setters in this implementation.

Deactivation removes event listeners; it does not send an explicit widget-removal command. Give temporary overlays an expiry and verify media-side context cleanup. Use the slide player's supported remove action for content that must be explicitly removed by GLF.

Source: scripts/src/commands/widget-player.vbs and scripts/src/bcp/bcp.vbs. Example: scripts/src/game/modes/inlaneshot.vbs in the example table; Dark Chaos also uses widgets in its base and feature modes.

docs.title: Build a complete timed mode
docs.text: This walkthrough combines qualification, a timer, progress, scoring and cleanup. It follows the component patterns used by the example table and Dark Chaos's double-scoring feature, using a small new rule: hit one target three times to start a 20-second challenge, then hit a second target five times to earn 100,000 points.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Use a working GLF table with game lifecycle and switch events already connected. Replace s_qualify_active and s_goal_active below with two actual switch events. No custom lights, sounds, player variables or media assets are required by this example.

Add the following sub to your game source and call CreateChallengeModes once from your configuration entry point before Glf_Init.

Sub CreateChallengeModes
    With CreateGlfMode("challenge_qualify", 300)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("challenge_qualified", "ball_will_end", "tilt")

        With .Counters("challenge_qualifier")
            .EnableEvents = Array("mode_challenge_qualify_started")
            .CountEvents = Array("s_qualify_active")
            .CountCompleteValue = 3
            .DisableOnComplete = True
            .ResetOnComplete = False
            .PersistState = False
            .EventsWhenComplete = Array("challenge_qualified")
        End With
    End With

    With CreateGlfMode("challenge", 400)
        .StartEvents = Array("challenge_qualified")
        .StopEvents = Array("challenge_finish", "challenge_timeout", "ball_will_end", "tilt")

        With .Counters("challenge_hits")
            .EnableEvents = Array("mode_challenge_started")
            .CountEvents = Array("s_goal_active")
            .CountCompleteValue = 5
            .DisableOnComplete = True
            .ResetOnComplete = False
            .PersistState = False
            .EventsWhenComplete = Array("challenge_complete")
        End With

        With .Timers("challenge_clock")
            .StartValue = 0
            .EndValue = 20
            .Direction = "up"
            .TickInterval = 1000
            With .ControlEvents()
                .EventName = "mode_challenge_started"
                .Action = "restart"
            End With
        End With

        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("challenge_complete.1")
                With .Variable("score")
                    .Action = "add"
                    .Int = 100000
                End With
            End With
        End With

        With .EventPlayer()
            .Add "challenge_complete", Array("challenge_finish")
            .Add "timer_challenge_clock_complete", Array("challenge_timeout")
        End With
    End With
End Sub

docs.title: Follow the event chain
docs.text:
Trigger Result ball_started Qualification starts with a fresh counter. Third qualifying hit Counter posts challenge_qualified; qualification stops and challenge starts. mode_challenge_started Enables the goal counter and restarts the timer. Fifth goal hit Posts challenge_complete; variable player awards points, then the event player posts challenge_finish. Timer completion Posts challenge_timeout; the mode stops without a completion award. Ball ending or tilt Both modes stop.

The .1 suffix raises that scoring listener's priority relative to the default listener in the same mode. It is not a delay. challenge_finish is deliberately separate from challenge_complete: award listeners get to process completion before mode teardown removes them.

Counter enable events are explicit because this counter implementation does not automatically begin counting on activation. PersistState = False resets progress when the mode is activated again. Qualification starts again on the next ball_started, so this version offers one challenge attempt per ball, including an extra ball.

docs.title: Add feedback and adapt the rule
docs.text:
Add a show player on mode_challenge_started and a completion effect on challenge_complete. Register shows before initialization. For displays, use segment displays or Godot slides. Give every repeating effect a defined stop or mode-cleanup path.

For progress that survives between balls, use player variables or a persistent shot/state-machine design. Do not simply add more start events: decide which counters should reset and when qualification becomes available again.

docs.title: Test the whole feature
docs.text:
Verify three qualifying hits start exactly one challenge; four goal hits do not award completion; the fifth awards exactly 100,000; timeout awards nothing; tilt and drain stop the timer; and the next player's qualification begins at zero. Also try a goal hit close to the timeout: event order determines which action is processed while the mode is still active.

Source: scripts/src/commands/counter.vbs, timer.vbs, mode.vbs, event-player.vbs and variable-player.vbs. For a larger feature, compare Dark Chaos's scripts/src/game/modes/double-scoring.vbs and the example table's scripts/src/game/modes/rampshot.vbs.

docs.title: Debugging game rules
docs.text: Follow one failing interaction from physical input to its final effect. Check the running table's bundled GLF version first: both example games carry their own scripts/src/glf/glf.vbs, which may differ from the framework source you are reading.

docs.title: Enable useful logging
docs.text:
Enable the table option Glf Debug Log, and use Glf Debug Log Level when more detail is needed. Make sure the table calls Glf_Options. Logs are written under the relative glf_logs folder with a filename beginning with cGameName and a timestamp.

Enable .Debug = True on the mode and the component being investigated where those objects expose it. Global logging alone does not make every component emit its optional detail. Debug initialization also exports MPF configuration; see Configuration and YAML before editing exported files.

Glf Monitor uses a separate BCP connection on port 5051 and requires the monitor/controller setup. Ordinary file logging is enough to begin investigating a rule.

docs.title: Trace one hit
docs.text:
1. Find the emitted switch event, such as s_RampHit_active. If absent, check the VPX object name, collection or specialized-device registration, generated handlers and tilt state.
  2. Find mode_<name>_started. Confirm the mode creation sub ran before Glf_Init, its start event happened and it has not already stopped.
  3. Find the listener for the rule event. Check exact spelling and whether conditions reference initialized variables or existing devices.
  4. Check priorities and intermediate events. An earlier handler may change a value, disable a device or stop a mode before a later action runs.
  5. Follow the effect to its target: a registered show, sound, light, ball device or media resource. A valid event with an unknown asset still cannot produce the expected result.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text:
Symptom Likely checks New code has no effect Rebuild the actual table script; confirm the table loads it and restart play YAML edit has no effect in VPX Mode YAML is exported; change the VBScript source. Show YAML must be converted again Mode starts but initialization is missed Use mode_<name>_started for that mode's players instead of the event that starts the mode Score awards twice Two active scoring handlers, duplicate switch dispatch, or overlapping unconditional/conditional mappings Expression fails at configuration time Quote runtime expressions, such as .Int = "1000 * current_player.multiplier" Counter never counts Give the counter an explicit enable event after its mode activates Progress belongs to the wrong player Separate player credit from shared machine/device state; verify index conventions Next ball never serves Find the queued event and missing WaitFor completion; also check trough/plunger state Saved initial value seems ignored The INI reload may override it; inspect the named variable's saved value Sound completion fires too soon Check the registered sound's duration and loop settings Media is blank Check BCP connection, mode context and resource names in the media project

The example table's watcher concatenates .vbs changes; it does not convert show YAML. Its production concatenation also includes cached-functions.vbs. Use the development workflow while changing expressions, and check the cache/build process if the generated script does not reflect the intended change.

docs.title: Verify cleanup and player boundaries
docs.text:
After fixing the normal path, exercise timeout, mode cancellation, tilt, drain, next player and a new game. Look for timers still posting events, repeating shows or sounds, held balls, stale shot states and duplicate listeners. A successful first hit is not enough to establish a feature's lifecycle.

For a reproducible report, record the table/GLF revision, active modes, event sequence, player/ball, relevant variable values, expected behavior and the smallest configuration excerpt that reproduces the issue.

Source: scripts/src/logs.vbs, pin-event-handlers.vbs, _.main.vbs and the component under investigation. Related: events, game lifecycle, player state.

docs.title: Displays and Godot integration
docs.text:
GLF supports table-light segment displays and a separate media controller connected over BCP. Use segment displays for VPX alphanumeric lights. Use slides and widgets for a Godot backbox presentation. Game rules remain in GLF; media assets and layouts live in the media project.

This guide follows the checked-in example table's godot/GMCDisplay project and GLF's BCP implementation. It is not a general installation guide for every version of GMC.

docs.title: Start from the supplied media project
docs.text:
1. Use the example table's godot/GMCDisplay/project.godot, which contains the bundled GMC add-on, slides/, widgets/, gmc.cfg and media resources. Keep that known combination working before upgrading the add-on.
  2. On the Windows VPX machine, install the example table's bcp-controller/VpxBcpController.msi if the vpx_bcp_controller.VpxBcpController COM component is not already registered.
  3. Run the media project and confirm its output reports that GMC is listening for BCP. The bundled server defaults to port 5050; its gmc.bcp_port configuration can override that.
  4. Match GLF's bcpPort, then enable the table option Glf Backbox Control Protocol. The table must already call Glf_Options, Glf_Init and Glf_Exit as described in installation.

docs.title: Choose how the media process starts
docs.text:
Set these existing globals after loading GLF and before the connection is requested; do not redeclare them with Dim:

glf_production_mode = False
bcpDebug = True
bcpPort = 5050

This development setup selects ConnectToDebug for an already running media project. To let the controller launch the editor/project instead, use glf_production_mode = False, bcpDebug = False, and supply bcpLocalPathToGodot and bcpLocalPathToProject for your machine.

In production mode, Glf_ConnectToBCPMediaController passes bcpExeName to ConnectToBuild. Set it to the built media executable/command expected by your controller setup. This checkout defaults it to cGameName & "_gmc"; the example table's bundled GLF uses a different startup implementation. Check the version actually included in your table instead of copying its defaults blindly.

The GLF monitor is a separate connection on port 5051. Enabling Glf Monitor does not connect the media controller on 5050.

docs.title: Play a slide
docs.text:
The example media project has a base slide. Inside your base mode:

With .SlidePlayer()
    With .EventName("mode_base_started")
        .Slide = "base"
        .Action = "play"
    End With
End With

The mode name, event name and slide resource name must match your project. The slide player sends its action, expiry, effective priority and event arguments to BCP. Mode stop sends a context clear for slides. Use an explicit slide remove action when removing a slide before the mode ends.

A widget player adds smaller overlays, such as the example table's left_spinner widget. GLF sends playback commands; defining a player entry does not create the Godot scene or register its resource.

docs.title: Player data and presentation lifetime
docs.text:
GLF sends player-add, current-player, player-variable and machine-variable messages. Bind display resources to the corresponding data in the supplied media project. Verify two-player scoring and player changes, rather than testing only player 1. After game end, live player state is cleared; final scores are retained in machine variables.

For transient effects, use a defined expiry. Do not let missing media playback block the game: a feature waiting for a presentation should have a game-side timer or skip path that can post its completion event.

docs.title: Diagnose a blank display
docs.text:
Observation Check COM/controller startup error Controller installation and the exact registered COM class Media project does not connect Listening port, running project and GLF debug/production startup branch Connection works but no slide appears Active mode, exact trigger name, resource registration and media logs Correct slide but old score Variable binding, player number and whether player-state messages arrive Overlay remains after a feature Expiry, slide context cleanup and the current widget-player limitations

Source: scripts/src/bcp/bcp.vbs, connection/options code in scripts/src/_.main.vbs, and commands/slide-player.vbs / widget-player.vbs. Working examples: example table scripts/src/game/modes/base.vbs, inlaneshot.vbs and godot/GMCDisplay.

docs.title: Game and ball lifecycle
docs.text: Use lifecycle events to decide how long a mode lives and when its state resets. The implementation is in scripts/src/game.vbs; event constants are defined in scripts/src/_.main.vbs.

docs.title: From start button to first ball
docs.text:
Event What it means for your rules request_to_start_game A start request is checked, including whether the trough contains the expected balls. Do not use it to award points. player_added A player is being added; kwargs.num is one-based. The event is posted as the player is created. game_start The game flag and first player have been set. Start game-long modes here. game_started Posted after a short startup delay. Player-state refresh and ball-release handlers run from here. balldevice_trough_ball_eject_attempt A queued ball-release event. A release carrying new_ball starts a new ball. ball_started The new ball is counted in play and is being served. Start per-ball rules and reset per-ball variables here.

ball_started is a serve-time event, not proof that the player has plunged or hit the playfield. Use a suitable playfield switch or your ball-save timer-start event for features that should begin only after launch.

docs.title: From drain to next player
docs.text:
An ordinary drain passes through the ball_drain relay. Saves and multiball handlers can consume the drain before the core game handler ends the ball. Do not end a ball from a raw drain switch hit.

When the last unclaimed ball drains, the core posts ball_will_end, then queues ball_ending. The low-priority end-of-ball handler posts ball_ended after higher-priority queued work is released. This is where bonus fits.

After ball_ended, an extra ball keeps the same player and ball number, consuming one extra_balls award. Otherwise the outgoing player's ball number increases and the current player advances. If the next player still has balls remaining, next_player leads to another ball release. Even an extra-ball serve uses this continuation path; the event name alone does not prove the player changed.

At the end of the game, the core posts game_will_end and queues game_ending. It copies final scores to machine variables, clears player state, then posts game_ended. Read final scores from the machine variables after this point, not current_player.

docs.title: Choose a mode lifetime
docs.text:
With CreateGlfMode("scoring", 2000)
    .StartEvents = Array("game_start")
    .StopEvents = Array("game_ended")
End With

With CreateGlfMode("base", 100)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
    .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
End With

These are setup excerpts; add components inside each mode. A feature that belongs to base can stop on mode_base_stopping. The example table's modes/score.vbs uses a game-long mode, while modes/multiball.vbs starts each ball and stops with base.

docs.title: Wait for bonus
docs.text:
The example table's scripts/src/game/modes/bonus.vbs uses:

With CreateGlfMode("bonus", 150)
    .StartEvents = Array("ball_ending{game.tilted == False}")
    .StopEvents = Array("bonus_finished")
    .UseWaitQueue = True
End With

Add the actual bonus calculation and presentation before using this excerpt. UseWaitQueue asks the queued start event to wait for mode_bonus_stopped. Every completion and skip path must eventually post bonus_finished; otherwise the next ball cannot proceed. Use a priority above the core ball_ending handler's 10 so the wait is installed before that handler runs.

Tilt has its own drain/settle handling in scripts/src/commands/tilt.vbs. Stop scoring features on tilt and use the condition above to skip bonus. Do not manually advance players to bypass a stalled queue; find the missing completion event.

docs.title: Game settings and verification
docs.text:
Use the table's Balls Per Game option to choose 3 Balls or 5 Balls. Glf_Init creates the game settings object with three balls, then calls Glf_Options, which applies that option. A separate settings call before initialization is overwritten; use the existing option for the supported choices. This is the number of turns per player, independent of tnob, the physical ball count.

Test a normal drain, saved drain, multiball drain, tilt, extra ball, two-player change and final game end. Confirm that progress resets at the intended boundary. See player state, queue relay player and debugging.

docs.title: Build a multiball feature
docs.text: A multiball lock tracks qualification; a multiball device manages balls in play and shoot-again. A physical ball device knows where a ball actually is. Keep those responsibilities separate, especially in a multi-player game.

docs.title: Start with virtual locks
docs.text:
Virtual locks credit progress without retaining a physical ball. This setup needs a working trough and auto-launch plunger. Call CreateDemoMultiball during configuration. Post qualify_demo_locks from a completed shot group or other qualification rule, then post demo_lock_hit from the shot that collects each lock.

Sub CreateDemoMultiball
    With CreateGlfMode("demo_mb", 1000)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")

        With .MultiballLocks("demo_locks")
            .EnableEvents = Array("qualify_demo_locks")
            .DisableEvents = Array("disable_demo_locks")
            .LockEvents = Array("demo_lock_hit")
            .ResetEvents = Array("prepare_demo_locks")
            .BallsToLock = 2
        End With

        With .Multiballs("demo")
            .StartEvents = Array("start_demo_mb")
            .BallCount = 3
            .BallCountType = "total"
            .ShootAgain = 15000
            .HurryUp = 3000
            .GracePeriod = 2000
        End With

        With .EventPlayer()
            .Add "qualify_demo_locks", Array("prepare_demo_locks")
            .Add "multiball_lock_demo_locks_full", Array("start_demo_mb")
            .Add "multiball_demo_started", Array("disable_demo_locks", "enable_demo_jackpots")
            .Add "multiball_demo_ended", Array("disable_demo_jackpots", "restart_demo_qualification")
        End With
    End With
End Sub

The lock's reset listener exists while the lock is enabled. Posting a separate prepare_demo_locks event after qualification allows it to reset the current player's lock count after enabling. Use plain event names in LockEvents and ResetEvents: this implementation registers those arrays directly rather than parsing event conditions or priority suffixes.

Three balls with BallCountType = "total" means a target of three in play, not three additional balls. Do not manually increment glf_BIP to launch multiball.

docs.title: Add jackpots and requalification
docs.text:
enable_demo_jackpots, disable_demo_jackpots and restart_demo_qualification above are hooks for your rules, not built-in GLF commands. One approach is a dedicated jackpot mode that starts on multiball_demo_started and stops on multiball_demo_ended, ball_will_end or tilt. Its variable player can score a jackpot switch only while that mode is active.

Keep the qualification rules disabled during multiball. On restart_demo_qualification, reset the qualification shots and allow the player to earn qualify_demo_locks again. For a feature that should be available only once per ball, leave qualification disabled until the next ball instead.

docs.title: Replace virtual locks with physical locks
docs.text:
Configure two ball devices, for example kicker1 and kicker2, with switches, eject callbacks and capacities appropriate to your table. In the lock configuration, replace LockEvents with:

.LockDevices = Array("kicker1", "kicker2")

In the multiball configuration, add:

.BallLocks = Array("kicker1", "kicker2")

The lock claims entering balls and schedules replacement balls when appropriate; the multiball releases the listed physical devices when it starts. Disable competing ball holds for those devices while locking. Qualification still determines when the lock is enabled.

Player lock credit is stored as <lock_name>_locked_balls. Physical occupancy belongs to the device and can differ from a player's credit. The example table's scripts/src/game/modes/multiball.vbs demonstrates stealable locks using machine occupancy variables, shot states and a state machine. Study that complete implementation before adding shared physical locks between players.

LockedBallCountingStrategy has a setter and export support, but the current runtime lock calculation does not branch on it. Do not assume selecting an MPF strategy name changes GLF behavior.

docs.title: End and shoot-again behavior
docs.text:
The multiball emits multiball_<name>_started, _shoot_again, _hurry_up, _grace_period, _shoot_again_ended, _ball_lost and _ended during its lifecycle. The drain-count handler posts _ended when the remaining global ball count would be one (or the game is no longer running). That normally returns to single-ball play; it does not end the player's ball.

Timing values above are milliseconds. Test drains during shoot-again, around its expiry, and after it ends. Test two players with different lock credit and physically occupied locks, and verify a new game does not inherit stale qualification. Check Multiball, Multiball Locks and source scripts/src/commands/multiball.vbs and multiball-locks.vbs for additional settings.

docs.title: Build your first GLF game
docs.text:
Build a small VPX table with one physical ball, three turns per player, a manual plunger, two flippers, one scoring rollover and general illumination. By the end of the core tutorial you can start a game, play, score, drain three times and start another game. A simple backglass text box displays the current player, ball and score; no external media controller is required.

This is a cumulative build. Keep one table script and one ConfigureGlfDevices sub. Each chapter tells you exactly which objects and subs to add. The first three chapters form the initial runnable setup; finish them before pressing Play.

docs.title: Core path
docs.text:
Chapter What you build Checkpoint 1. Empty table and script Required objects, collections and GLF loading Names and hooks are ready 2. Physical trough Ball storage and return path One ball can return to the release kicker 3. Plunger and first serve Shooter lane, tracking and launch Start serves a ball; drain serves the next 4. Flippers Both flipper callbacks Flippers work during a ball and release at ball end 5. Score and display One rollover, score rule and text display One pass scores 1,000 for the current player 6. Lights and complete-game test GI controlled by a mode Complete three turns and start a new game

The completed core script is a comparison/reference file for chapters 1–6. It does not create VPX geometry or replace the object setup below. It has been checked against GLF source, but the new tutorial has not yet been play-tested in VPX. Existing .vpx files in the repository's tutorial/ folder are older geometry references, not validated snapshots of this new script.

docs.title: One naming scheme
docs.text:
VPX object Type / settings Collection Table1 Table with a sloped playfield, outlanes and shooter lane — swTrough1 Capturing kicker at the trough release position None; GLF owns its handlers Drain Capturing kicker reached by all drained balls None; GLF owns its handlers Plunger Mechanical plunger facing up the shooter lane None s_plunger Trigger covered by a resting ball at the plunger glf_switches LeftFlipper, RightFlipper Flippers with mirrored start/end angles None s_score Rollover trigger on the playfield glf_switches l_gi Light, initially off, BlinkPattern GI glf_lights Glf_GameTimer Timer, Enabled, Interval -1 None; GLF owns its timer sub TutorialDisplayTimer Timer, Enabled, Interval 100 None ScoreText Backglass TextBox, visible in desktop view None

Create empty glf_slingshots and glf_spinners collections as well. Keep collection event generation disabled: GLF generates the individual switch handlers. Do not add the trough or drain kickers to glf_switches and do not write duplicate _Hit or _UnHit subs for registered objects.

docs.title: Extend the working game
docs.text:
After chapter 6, add these in order or select the independent optional devices:

  1. Event routing: separate a physical switch from its award.
  2. Ball save: save one early drain and automatically launch the replacement.
  3. Shot progress: light an insert and score a completed objective.
  4. Timed opportunity: light a timed award window.
  5. Optional scoop: capture and return a ball.
  6. Optional autofire device: add a simple kickback.

Advanced modes, multiball, sound, Godot, tilt and high scores follow after this core loop. See the learning guides. This tutorial uses local VBScript configuration; exported YAML is explained separately in Configuration and YAML.

Tutorial map · Next

docs.title: 12. Optional autofire: a simple kickback
docs.text:
Goal: show how an autofire device connects a switch event to a physical action. This example uses a kicker so the callback can be complete without importing a sling animation or physics system.

Add a capturing Kicker named s_kickback in a return lane where its kick will send the ball back onto the playfield. Add it to glf_switches. Do not also register it as a GLF ball device: this example uses immediate autofire behavior.

Add these subs and append ConfigureTutorialKickback to ConfigureGlfDevices:

Sub ConfigureTutorialKickback()
    With CreateGlfAutoFireDevice("tutorial_kickback")
        .Switch = "s_kickback"
        .ActionCallback = "TutorialKickbackAction"
    End With
End Sub

Sub TutorialKickbackAction(args)
    If args(0) = 1 And s_kickback.BallCntOver > 0 Then
        s_kickback.Kick 0, 20
    End If
End Sub

Autofire action callbacks receive an array: args(0) is the enabled/action state and args(1) is the active ball, when available. This differs from the flipper callback's Boolean and ball-device eject callback's ball argument. The callback above acts only on activation and checks physical occupancy.

Defaults enable the device on ball_started and disable it on ball_will_end / service entry. The kick direction and speed must match your return lane. This basic exercise does not implement kickback qualification or a one-use limit.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
During a ball, send the ball into the kicker and confirm it returns to play once, without changing the player/ball number. Make sure its unhit event does not kick again. At ball end the autofire device should disable.

Slingshots and bumpers use the same GLF device type, but their callbacks must drive their own VPX mechanics/animations. Add real slingshots to glf_slingshots; do not copy undefined LeftSlingshotAction or enable/disable callback names from another table. For the full pattern, inspect the example table's _configuration.vbs and matching VPX physics files.

Your next steps are a complete game mode, multiball, tilt, sound, displays and high scores. Keep the core acceptance test working as each feature is added.

Previous · Tutorial map

docs.title: 11. Optional scoop: capture and return a ball
docs.text:
Prerequisite: the core game is working. This optional device does not depend on the shots or timer extensions.

Add a capturing Kicker named s_scoop on the playfield and put it in glf_switches. Place it so a kick toward the upper playfield clears nearby walls. Keep its hit/unhit subs free for GLF's generated switch handlers.

Add these subs and append ConfigureTutorialScoop to ConfigureGlfDevices:

Sub ConfigureTutorialScoop()
    With CreateGlfBallDevice("tutorial_scoop")
        .BallSwitches = Array("s_scoop")
        .EjectTimeout = 2000
        .EjectCallback = "TutorialScoopEject"
    End With
End Sub

Sub TutorialScoopEject(ball)
    If IsObject(ball) Then s_scoop.Kick 0, 15
End Sub

Adjust the kick angle and strength to your scoop geometry. The callback returns the existing ball; it must not destroy and recreate it.

With no hold or lock claiming it, an unexpected ball is automatically ejected by the device after entry handling. balldevice_tutorial_scoop_ball_enter is the claim relay used by holds/locks; balldevice_tutorial_scoop_ball_entered is the notification event suitable for an award. The latter can be mapped to tutorial_score_1000 inside the scoring mode's event player if you completed chapter 7.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
A ball entering the scoop should settle, eject and continue playing without changing the current ball number. The device should recognize its exit. If the ball stays captured, check the callback, unclaimed-ball handling and physical kick path. A ball-save should not be needed for an ordinary scoop return.

To hold the ball during a selection or presentation, add a ball hold with an explicit release event. A scoop does not automatically wait for an arbitrary award animation to finish.

Previous · Tutorial map · Next

docs.title: 8. Save one early drain
docs.text:
Prerequisite: the core game serves and drains reliably, and TutorialPlungerEject(ball) from chapter 3 is present. Keep the ball count at one for this exercise.

Add this sub, then append CreateTutorialBallSave to the existing ConfigureGlfDevices:

Sub CreateTutorialBallSave()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_save", 150)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .BallSaves("tutorial_save")
            .EnableEvents = Array("mode_tutorial_save_started")
            .TimerStartEvents = Array("balldevice_plunger_ball_eject_success")
            .ActiveTime = 10000
            .HurryUpTime = 2000
            .GracePeriod = 1000
            .BallsToSave = 1
            .AutoLaunch = True
        End With
    End With
End Sub

The mode enables the save when the new ball starts. Its timer begins when the plunger device confirms a successful exit. That confirmation follows the configured eject timeout, rather than the exact instant the plunger key is released. Durations here are milliseconds; the grace period extends the nominal active period.

BallsToSave = 1 limits this save to one drain. AutoLaunch = True uses the plunger device's callback for the replacement ball. With only one physical ball, it must first return to the trough before it can be served again. GLF handles that wait; do not create another ball or manipulate the ball-in-play counter.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Launch and drain promptly. The replacement should be served and automatically launched without advancing the displayed player or ball number. Drain that replacement: this save has been used, so normal ball-end handling should occur. On the next ball, launch and keep it alive until the save and grace time have elapsed; a subsequent drain must advance to the next turn.

If the replacement sits at the plunger, check the eject callback and its lane direction. If a drain never advances, check that you did not set unlimited saves or restart the save on every hit. Repeat the chapter 6 full-game test with the new behavior understood.

Reference: Ball Save.

docs.title: 7. Separate switch events from awards
docs.text:
Prerequisite: finish the core game through chapter 6. This chapter changes the existing scoring sub; it does not create a second scoring mode.

Replace CreateTutorialScoring with the following version. Keep its existing call in ConfigureGlfDevices exactly once.

Sub CreateTutorialScoring()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_scoring", 100)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .EventPlayer()
            .Add "s_score_active", Array("tutorial_score_1000")
        End With
        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("tutorial_score_1000")
                With .Variable("score")
                    .Action = "add"
                    .Int = 1000
                End With
            End With
        End With
    End With
End Sub

Now the path is s_score_active → tutorial_score_1000 → score increment. Other devices can post tutorial_score_1000 without repeating the scoring rule. Later, another player can also listen to the same award event for sound or display feedback.

Remove the old s_score_active variable-player entry when applying this replacement. Keeping both gives 2,000 points per rollover. Do not create another CreateTutorialScoring sub or add the same event key twice to one event player.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
A single rollover still awards exactly 1,000. Drain, start another ball and check the route still works. With debug logging enabled, follow the switch event and then the award event. See Events for conditions, event arguments and priority offsets after this simple path works.

Previous · Tutorial map · Next

docs.title: 4. Make both flippers playable
docs.text:
Goal: control both flippers during an active ball and release them at ball end.

Name the VPX objects LeftFlipper and RightFlipper, position them above the drain, and mirror their start/end angles so they flip toward the playfield. GLF supplies input events named s_left_flipper and s_right_flipper; these are keyboard-derived switches, not extra VPX Trigger objects.

docs.title: Add both callbacks
docs.text:
Sub ConfigureTutorialFlippers()
    With CreateGlfFlipper("left")
        .Switch = "s_left_flipper"
        .ActionCallback = "TutorialLeftFlipper"
    End With
    With CreateGlfFlipper("right")
        .Switch = "s_right_flipper"
        .ActionCallback = "TutorialRightFlipper"
    End With
End Sub

Sub TutorialLeftFlipper(enabled)
    If enabled Then
        LeftFlipper.RotateToEnd
    Else
        LeftFlipper.RotateToStart
    End If
End Sub

Sub TutorialRightFlipper(enabled)
    If enabled Then
        RightFlipper.RotateToEnd
    Else
        RightFlipper.RotateToStart
    End If
End Sub

Append ConfigureTutorialFlippers after ConfigureTutorialPlunger inside the existing ConfigureGlfDevices. Keep the same two key handlers from chapter 1. Do not add direct flipper rotation there as well.

The flipper device defaults enable it on ball_started and disable it on ball_will_end or service_mode_entered. Keeping those defaults avoids relying on a custom kill_flippers event that this game never posts. These simple callbacks demonstrate GLF wiring; advanced flipper physics can replace their internals later.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Before Start, the flippers should remain at rest. Start and launch a ball: both buttons should move their respective flippers and release correctly. Drain while holding a button and confirm both return to rest. Test another ball to confirm they enable again. Correct mirrored angles or collision geometry in the editor if a callback runs but the ball cannot be played.

Reference: Flipper API.

docs.title: 6. Add GI and finish a complete game
docs.text:
Goal: light the playfield during a ball and verify the complete game loop before adding more features.

Add a Light named l_gi, initially off, and include it in glf_lights. Set its BlinkPattern field to GI. GLF uses this field for comma-separated tags; additional GI lights can share that tag. Keep the tag exactly consistent with the rule.

docs.title: Add the GI mode
docs.text:
Sub CreateTutorialLights()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_lights", 100)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .LightPlayer()
            With .EventName("mode_tutorial_lights_started")
                With .Lights("GI")
                    .Color = "ffffff"
                End With
            End With
        End With
    End With
End Sub

Append CreateTutorialLights to ConfigureGlfDevices. The complete core configuration entry point is now:

Sub ConfigureGlfDevices()
    ConfigureTutorialPlunger
    ConfigureTutorialFlippers
    CreateTutorialScoring
    CreateTutorialLights
End Sub

The light player responds to its own mode's started event, when its listeners are ready. Stopping the mode removes its light entry; with no other light rule active, the GI returns to its off baseline.

docs.title: Acceptance test: one complete game
docs.text:
1. Start the table: one physical ball is in the trough, GI is off and the display says PRESS START.
  2. Press and release Start: a ball is served, GI turns on and the display shows player 1, ball 1, score 0.
  3. Launch, flip and cross s_score twice: score becomes 2,000.
  4. Drain: the ball returns through the trough; ball 2 is served and the score remains 2,000.
  5. Drain balls 2 and 3. With the table's Balls Per Game option set to 3 Balls, no fourth ball is served. GI turns off and PRESS START returns.
  6. Start a fresh game: score and ball number reset. Confirm there is still only one physical ball.
  7. Start another game, add player 2 with Start during ball 1, and verify separate scores and alternating turns after drains.

The table option can select five balls, so check it if your game continues after the third drain. Physical ball count (tnob) is independent of turns per game.

Compare your script with the completed core script. It includes chapters 1–6 only. Do not append it below your existing script; use it to compare or replace the whole tutorial script after saving a copy.

You now have the core loop. Add features only after these checks pass; otherwise debugging a new rule becomes mixed up with physical ball-routing problems.

docs.title: 3. Serve and launch the first ball
docs.text:
Goal: start a game, serve a ball and launch it into the playfield.

Create a mechanical VPX plunger named Plunger at the foot of the right-hand shooter lane. Place a Trigger named s_plunger where the ball rests against it, and add that trigger to glf_switches. The resting ball must keep the trigger active; launching must let it leave the trigger.

The old illustration uses sw01; use s_plunger throughout this tutorial. Ensure the lane opens into the playfield and a launched ball cannot immediately escape the table.

docs.title: Add configuration and callback
docs.text:
Add these subs outside all other subs:

Sub ConfigureTutorialPlunger()
    With CreateGlfBallDevice("plunger")
        .BallSwitches = Array("s_plunger")
        .DefaultDevice = True
        .MechanicalEject = True
        .EjectTimeout = 2000
        .EjectCallback = "TutorialPlungerEject"
    End With
End Sub

Sub TutorialPlungerEject(ball)
    If IsObject(ball) Then
        ball.VelX = 0
        ball.VelY = -45
    End If
End Sub

Replace the empty ConfigureGlfDevices body with:

Sub ConfigureGlfDevices()
    ConfigureTutorialPlunger
End Sub

DefaultDevice = True identifies the destination of trough serves. MechanicalEject = True allows the ball to leave under manual plunger power. The two-second timeout is the interval used to confirm a mechanical exit; it does not launch the ball.

The callback supplies a simple automatic launch for the later ball-save chapter, using a shooter lane directed toward decreasing Y. It is deliberately separate from manual Plunger.Fire. Adjust the velocity for your geometry if necessary; never replace the ball. A pulse callback can receive Null, so the object check matters.

docs.title: First runtime checkpoint
docs.text:
Press Play, wait for initialization, then press and release the configured Start key. GLF checks the trough and starts the game on the key-up request. Exactly one ball should appear at the plunger. Hold and release the configured plunger key to launch it. The flippers are not wired yet, so let the ball drain.

Repeat the serve/drain cycle. The physical ball should return to the trough, and GLF should serve the next turn. After the third unsaved drain, the game should stop serving until Start is pressed again. The score display is added in chapter 5.

If the ball is served but GLF never sees it at the plunger, check trigger coverage, spelling and collection membership. If it cannot reach the playfield, correct lane geometry and plunger settings before adding scoring. If it cannot return to swTrough1, fix the trough route.

Previous · Tutorial map · Next

docs.title: 5. Add scoring and a visible display
docs.text:
Goal: make one physical rollover award exactly 1,000 points and show the current player, ball and score.

Add a Trigger named s_score somewhere a launched ball can cross it and put it in glf_switches. Use a rollover rather than a standup target for this first rule; specialized target integration comes later.

docs.title: Register a scoring mode
docs.text:
Sub CreateTutorialScoring()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_scoring", 100)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("s_score_active")
                With .Variable("score")
                    .Action = "add"
                    .Int = 1000
                End With
            End With
        End With
    End With
End Sub

Append CreateTutorialScoring to ConfigureGlfDevices. This mode starts every ball and stops before ball-end processing. Its variable player listens to the generated s_score_active event. GLF creates the built-in score variable for each new player; do not initialize or reset it on every ball.

docs.title: Show the score without external media
docs.text:
Create a visible backglass TextBox named ScoreText and a Timer named TutorialDisplayTimer, Enabled with Interval 100. Add its callback:

Sub TutorialDisplayTimer_Timer()
    If glf_gameStarted And Not IsNull(glf_currentPlayer) Then
        ScoreText.Text = "PLAYER " & CStr(GetPlayerState("number")) & _
            "   BALL " & CStr(GetPlayerState("ball")) & _
            "   SCORE " & CStr(GetPlayerState("score"))
    Else
        ScoreText.Text = "PRESS START"
    End If
End Sub

Test in desktop view with the backglass TextBox visible. This small UI timer only reads state; it does not run the game or score points. Glf_GameTimer must still run independently.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Start a new game and verify PLAYER 1, BALL 1, SCORE 0. Cross the rollover once: the score becomes 1,000. Cross again after leaving the trigger: 2,000. Drain and confirm the next ball retains the score. Do not leave the rollover inside the shooter-lane trigger or another overlapping sensor.

If a hit scores twice, look for duplicate hit subs or a second scoring rule. If there is no score, confirm collection membership and that mode_tutorial_scoring_started occurred. If points change but the text does not, check the display timer and backglass visibility separately.

We will replace this direct switch-to-score mapping with an event player in the optional event-routing chapter. For now, keep one award source. Reference: Variable Player.
