docs.title: 1. Prepare the empty table
docs.text:
Goal: prepare a new table and a single script that subsequent chapters extend.

Use VPX with the scripting features used by this GLF checkout, including Table1.Option. Save a new table as GLFFirstGame.vpx and name the table object Table1. Begin with simple, visible geometry: perimeter walls, two flippers, an open drain below them, and a shooter lane on the right that feeds the upper playfield. Keep the lane wide enough for a 50-unit-diameter ball, with clearance rather than a tight fit.

If starting from VPX's default new-table template, remove its sample game script and old ball creation/drain logic. Keep only the physical pieces you want and rename them to the object list. You do not need artwork, ROM code, sound, B2S, Godot or a script watcher to complete this tutorial.

docs.title: Editor setup
docs.text:
Create the four collections glf_lights, glf_switches, glf_slingshots and glf_spinners in the collection manager. Add the timers and backglass TextBox from the object list. Put ScoreText on the backglass and test in desktop view so it is visible. Leave the display timer disabled until chapter 5 if its callback is not yet in your script.

Use the framework build scripts/vpx-glf.vbs from your GLF checkout and put it in VPX's Scripts folder, alongside the installed standard scripts. Load it only once. Define the table constants before loading GLF because GLF reads tnob and cGameName during script execution.

docs.title: Initial script
docs.text:
Paste this into the table's script editor. Leave one empty configuration sub for chapter 3:

Const cGameName = "GLFFirstGame"
Const BallSize = 50
Const BallMass = 1
Const tnob = 1
Const lob = 0
Dim gBot
Dim tablewidth : tablewidth = Table1.Width
Dim tableheight : tableheight = Table1.Height

ExecuteGlobal GetTextFile("controller.vbs")
ExecuteGlobal GetTextFile("core.vbs")
ExecuteGlobal GetTextFile("vpx-glf.vbs")

Sub Table1_Init()
    ConfigureGlfDevices
    Glf_Init Table1
End Sub

Sub Table1_Exit()
    Glf_Exit
End Sub

Sub Table1_KeyDown(ByVal keycode)
    Glf_KeyDown keycode
    If keycode = PlungerKey Then Plunger.Pullback
End Sub

Sub Table1_KeyUp(ByVal keycode)
    Glf_KeyUp keycode
    If keycode = PlungerKey Then Plunger.Fire
End Sub

Sub Table1_OptionEvent(ByVal eventId)
    Glf_Options eventId
End Sub

Sub ConfigureGlfDevices()
    ' Chapter 3 adds the plunger; later chapters append more calls.
End Sub

controller.vbs and core.vbs come with the VPX installation. Do not suppress load errors: a missing GLF or core script must be fixed before continuing. GLF provides Glf_GameTimer_Timer, trough handlers and generated switch handlers; do not paste copies of them into this script.

tnob = 1 means one physical ball. It does not mean a one-ball game: the same ball is reused over three player turns. lob = 0 means no captive balls. Glf_Init creates the physical ball and fills gBot; do not create another ball in your own initialization.

Glf_KeyDown/Glf_KeyUp handle GLF inputs, while the explicit Plunger.Pullback/Plunger.Fire calls move the VPX plunger. Defining an eject callback alone does not wire keyboard plunger operation.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Before Play, finish the trough and plunger in chapters 2–3. At that point the table must have every referenced object, a default GLF ball device and one call to Glf_Init. Keep Glf Monitor and Glf Backbox Control Protocol off for this tutorial. If the table reports a missing object or unsupported Option method, resolve the setup/version mismatch before adding rules.

docs.title: 9. Add a shot with visible progress
docs.text:
Goal: one new target lights an insert and awards 5,000 points only on its first hit each ball.

Create a rollover Trigger called s_target and a Light called l_target beside it. Add the trigger to glf_switches and the light to glf_lights. Keep this separate from the s_score rollover so the two awards are easy to distinguish.

Add this sub and append CreateTutorialTarget to ConfigureGlfDevices:

Sub CreateTutorialTarget()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_target_mode", 200)
        .StartEvents = Array("ball_started")
        .StopEvents = Array("ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .ShotProfiles("tutorial_target_profile")
            .AdvanceOnHit = True
            With .States("unlit")
                .Show = "off"
            End With
            With .States("lit")
                .Show = "on"
            End With
        End With
        With .Shots("tutorial_target")
            .Switch = "s_target"
            .Profile = "tutorial_target_profile"
            .Persist = False
            With .Tokens()
                .Add "lights", "l_target"
            End With
        End With
        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("tutorial_target_unlit_hit")
                With .Variable("score")
                    .Action = "add"
                    .Int = 5000
                End With
            End With
        End With
    End With
End Sub

The profile defines states in order: index 0 is unlit, index 1 is lit. Profiles do not loop in this implementation; ProfileLoop is read-only, so do not assign it. GLF provides the off and on shows, and the shot supplies their required lights token. The API is .Shots("name"), not .Shot.

On a hit, GLF advances the profile and emits events describing the state before the hit. Therefore tutorial_target_unlit_hit awards completion on the first hit, while the insert changes to lit. Further hits emit tutorial_target_lit_hit and do not match this award. Persist = False lets this standalone tutorial shot start fresh on its next activation.

HitEvents is an input that tells a shot to register a hit from another event; it is not a list of awards to emit. Put scoring in a variable player responding to the shot's emitted events.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
At ball start the insert is off. First target pass: insert on and +5,000. Second pass: no additional target award. Drain and start another ball: insert off and the first target hit can earn the award again. Confirm player 2 starts unlit as well.

Once this works, continue with shot groups for sets of objectives and sequence shots for ramps/orbits that require ordered switches. Those need extra playfield objects and are not prerequisites for the core game.

docs.title: 10. Add a timed award opportunity
docs.text:
Goal: crossing the original scoring rollover opens a 15-second window; crossing a new goal during that window awards 10,000.

Add Trigger s_goal to glf_switches and Light l_window to glf_lights. Add the sub below and append CreateTutorialHurry to ConfigureGlfDevices. This works alongside the existing scoring mode: s_score still gives its ordinary 1,000 points.

Sub CreateTutorialHurry()
    With CreateGlfMode("tutorial_hurry", 300)
        .StartEvents = Array("s_score_active{modes.tutorial_hurry.active == False}")
        .StopEvents = Array("tutorial_hurry_finish", "timer_tutorial_hurry_clock_complete", "ball_will_end", "tilt")
        With .Timers("tutorial_hurry_clock")
            .StartValue = 0
            .EndValue = 15
            .Direction = "up"
            .TickInterval = 1000
            With .ControlEvents()
                .EventName = "mode_tutorial_hurry_started"
                .Action = "restart"
            End With
        End With
        With .LightPlayer()
            With .EventName("mode_tutorial_hurry_started")
                With .Lights("l_window")
                    .Color = "00ff00"
                End With
            End With
        End With
        With .VariablePlayer()
            With .EventName("s_goal_active.1")
                With .Variable("score")
                    .Action = "add"
                    .Int = 10000
                End With
            End With
        End With
        With .EventPlayer()
            .Add "s_goal_active", Array("tutorial_hurry_finish")
        End With
    End With
End Sub

The start condition prevents repeated rollover hits from restarting an already active mode. Its timer is named tutorial_hurry_clock, so its completion event is exactly timer_tutorial_hurry_clock_complete. The configuration API is .Timers, and the one-second tick interval makes 15 ticks a 15-second opportunity.

The goal awards points before posting a separate finish event. The .1 suffix raises that scoring listener's priority; it is not a time delay. Stopping the mode removes the light entry and timer activity. The goal is not scored outside the mode because its variable player is inactive.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
Before opening a window, s_goal gives no hurry-up award. Hit s_score: the green window light turns on. Hit s_score again during the window: it still gives the ordinary rollover score but does not extend the window. Hit s_goal in time: +10,000 and the light turns off. Try again and wait: expiry turns the light off with no hurry-up award. Drain during the window and verify it is gone on the next ball.

Timer control values have action-specific meanings. For example, add uses ticks, while pause uses a delay. Consult the Timer API before adding controls; do not pass 5,000 expecting an addition of five ticks.

docs.title: 2. Build the physical trough
docs.text:
Goal: route the same physical ball from the drain back to the shooter lane without destroying it during play.

This tutorial uses tnob = 1: one release kicker called swTrough1 and a separate collecting kicker called Drain. Place them under/behind the apron with walls separating the trough from the live playfield. Both must capture balls. Funnel both outlanes and the centre drain into Drain.

The illustrations show a larger trough. For this tutorial, retain only the Drain → swTrough1 → shooter-lane route. Position the release kicker so its ejection reaches the bottom of the shooter lane and the ball settles onto s_plunger.

docs.title: Match the built-in kick directions
docs.text:
The checked-in trough code moves the ball using Drain.Kick 57, 10 into the last trough slot and swTrough1.Kick 90, 10 toward the shooter lane. Build the route to suit those directions; placing kickers anywhere on the table will not create a functioning trough. Use the old tutorial/glf_tutorial_trough.vpx as a geometry reference if you need to inspect the arrangement in VPX. Verify the route with visible kickers before hiding it under the apron.

For larger troughs, intermediate slots use swTrough2 through swTrough7. The eight-ball case also stores a ball in Drain; do not extrapolate a nonexistent swTrough8. Stay with one ball until the core game works.

docs.title: Script ownership
docs.text:
There is no CreateGlfBallDevice call for the built-in trough. Glf_Init creates one ball at swTrough1, sets the last trough slot and populates gBot. GLF already defines Drain_Hit, Drain_UnHit, swTrough1_Hit and swTrough1_UnHit.

Do not put these kickers in glf_switches, write another drain handler, or destroy/recreate balls on each drain. The current trough uses SetDelay for its update; a separate UpdateTroughTimer is not needed despite an old comment in the source.

docs.title: Checkpoint after chapter 3
docs.text:
The trough can be tested once the default plunger device is registered. At startup, one ball must sit in swTrough1. Start must release that ball to the shooter lane. A later drain must enter Drain, transfer to the vacated swTrough1, and become available for the next serve. If start is rejected, check actual trough occupancy first; the game will not start with a missing ball.
